## API Boundaries

Signatures are GDScript (typed). They restate the GDD contracts at the boundary; the GDD anchor in brackets is the authority.

### Kernel ingress and registration [command-simulation-layer CR-4..CR-10, CR-19]

```gdscript
# Ingress: a method of SurfaceHandle (ADR-0002), issued once at BOOTING to the Input Adapter by
# kernel.issue_surface_handle(&"input_adapter"). Fire-and-forget: returns nothing, calls nothing.
func submit(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, actor: int = NO_ACTOR, correlation: int = 0) -> void
# SYSTEM-origin submission from a step hook or apply (dedupe optional); on HookContext and ApplyContext only.
func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void

# Registration — methods of the module's BlockRegistrar (ModuleFacet.registrar, ADR-0003); legal only in
# BOOTING, set to null at the freeze; violations fail boot.
func register_block(desc: BlockDescriptor) -> void       # block_id, owner, schema_version, class, persist,
                                                          # persist_scope, scope, gameplay, interpolated,
                                                          # repl_hint, restore_after, callables
func register_command(desc: CommandTypeDescriptor) -> void  # allowed_origins, actor_binding, actor_source,
                                                          # coalesce, max_age_ticks, allowed_when_paused, writes_blocks
func register_hook(desc: HookDescriptor) -> void          # hook_id, owner_name, divisor, offset,
                                                          # after: [{id, tolerates_stale}], callable
func register_key_space(desc: KeySpaceDescriptor) -> void   # dirty-key layout (ADR-0004 § 3)

# Subscription — a method of a class-bound facet, not of the kernel (ADR-0004): NotifyFacet is held by the
# composition root (the subscriber class is fixed at issue); presenters hold PresentationFacet (ADR-0009).
# handler(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken
func subscribe(block_id: StringName, handler: Callable, name: StringName) -> SubscriptionHandle
```

*(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0002 / ADR-0003 / ADR-0004 sync)* There is no `Kernel` global (ADR-0001 § 5): the composition root (`src/game/game.gd`) hands each module the narrowest facet through `setup(facet)`. Control-plane requests (`request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, seat binding) are methods of a `ControlHandle` issued to the named callers only (`save_load`, `pause_gate`, `game.gd`), not commands. `request_restore(payload: Dictionary, restore_epoch: int, expected_state_hash: int = 0, has_expected_hash: bool = false) -> void` returns a verdict `NONE` when `has_expected_hash` is `false` (ADR-0002 § 6).

**Invariants callers respect:** never construct a command with `issuer_peer`; payloads hold only whitelisted Variant types (finite floats, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 4 KiB, no Object/Callable/NodePath/RID); never submit from a PRESENTATION handler. **Kernel guarantees:** exactly one terminal result per command; apply order ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`; subscribers see only post-P4 state.

### Owner-callable contract [CR-19, ruling R3]

```gdscript
# Every kernel-invoked owner callable receives a ctx and returns only ctx.complete().
func validate(cmd: Command, views: ReadViews, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken:
	if not _target_exists(cmd.payload):
		ctx.reject(&"NO_SUCH_TARGET")
		return ctx.complete()
	ctx.ok()
	return ctx.complete()

func apply(cmd: Command, scope: WriteScope, ctx: ApplyContext) -> CompletionToken
func snapshot(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken           # ctx.put(plain_dictionary)
func restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken
func post_restore(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken
func read_view(ctx: Object) -> CompletionToken
```

⚠️ `CompletionToken` return — Godot 4.7 (post-cutoff; HIGH only if owners are subclasses). The 4.7 rule (an override of a typed method inherits its return type and needs an explicit `return`) applies **only if** owner callables override a base class such as `BlockOwner`. ADR-0003 (Proposed) chose registered `Callable`s on plain (normally `RefCounted`) owners with no base class, so the rule is moot for owner methods and GDScript's ordinary "a typed function returns on every path" check applies; its context classes override nothing. *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0003 sync)* Either way the kernel checks the returned token's identity with a real `if`, never an `assert`, because `assert` is stripped from release exports (KRN-CTX-06). Verified against `docs/engine-reference/godot/breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 → 4.7 (GDScript). Behaviour confirmed: NEEDS VERIFICATION on a release export.

### Mutator contract [CR-9, LS-18, LY-27, BDY-21]

```gdscript
# Class A: pure check + infallible apply. The caller's validate runs the check.
func check_weld_join(plan: JoinPlan) -> StringName                # &"" = OK, else a reason
func weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int   # status OK / REFUSED / -code; fills caller-owned out {seam_id, opening_ids} (ADR-0003 § 5)
# Class B: clamps, never rejects, no-ops on stale ids; returns void (ADR-0003 § 5).
func push_stimulus(scope: WriteScope, kind: int, source_ref: int, cls: NoiseClass) -> void
# Cross-system Class A mutators called inside one apply return a status the caller must check.
func rebase_on_attach(scope: WriteScope, surviving: int, absorbed: int, frame_shift_px: Vector2i) -> int  # MutatorStatus.OK, REFUSED, or -fault_code (ADR-0003 § 5)
```

Mutators mark their own dirty keys explicitly (4.7 packed-array element writes call no setter). A mutator called outside a kernel WriteScope writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, and reports a violation.

### Read views [CR-12, LS-19, EM-25]

```gdscript
# Getter-only facade or deep copy; never a live container. Hot paths use typed scalar getters
# or caller-owned buffers and allocate nothing per call.
func compartment_p(cid: int) -> int
func failures(filter: FailureFilter, out: FailureSlice) -> void
func rects_in(aabb: Rect2i, out: QueryBuffer) -> void             # Layout OccluderSource
func solid_in(body_id: int, aabb: Rect2i, out: QueryBuffer) -> void
func lit(ref: int) -> bool                                        # Emitter, hysteresis on act_lux_pm
```

Any simulation-side read of a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block returns an empty view and counts `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`.

### Pure simulation functions shared across systems

```gdscript
class_name LocomotionStep extends RefCounted   # Body BDY-10; reused by Horror
static func step(state: LocoState, intent: LocoIntent, collide: SolidQuery) -> LocoResult
static func step_into(state: LocoState, intent: LocoIntent, collide: SolidQuery, out: LocoResult) -> void

# Kernel D.10 — pure, golden-vector pinned
static func rng_derive(world_seed: int, stream_name: StringName, counter: int) -> int
static func rng_derive_epoch(world_seed: int, stream_name: StringName, counter: int, restore_epoch: int) -> int
```

### Perception Filter [PF-*]

```gdscript
# The only path from a true value to a corruptible display. Pull query; no block, no hook.
func perceived(ref: PerceptionRef, viewer: int) -> Perceived
# PerceptionRef kinds: GRAPH_NODE, GRAPH_COMPARTMENT, SUIT_KEY, SCANNER, HOUSING_GLOW, STATE_GLYPH, MACHINE_FRAME
```

**Guarantees:** a ref whose tag is a truth channel always returns the true value; with no active lie the result equals the true value; the Filter writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material` and `Light2D` properties and its decoy list.

### Presentation subscriber contract [PIPE PR-20, LO-1]

```gdscript
# Handler: a method Callable on a long-lived object (no lambda, no .bind()); never awaits (ADR-0004, ADR-0009 § 2).
func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:  # marks dirty only; no draw, no read of other blocks
	_dirty.absorb(batch)                               # DirtyAccumulator (ADR-0004); a Dictionary.merge of a packed array was never valid
	return ctx.complete()                              # ADR-0003 callable contract, ADR-0009 § 2

# Presenters define no _process. PresentationDriver calls present(frame) once per frame, from PipelineRoot's single
# _process, in stage order (ADR-0009 § 3). Reads committed views at frame.alpha.
func present(frame: PresentFrame) -> void:
	if _dirty.is_empty() and not _animating():         # early-out only when both dirty and animating are empty (ADR-0009 § 2):
		return                                         # interpolation needs a draw on frames with no notification
	_redraw(frame.alpha)                               # alpha is frame.alpha, read once per frame; never Kernel.tick_alpha
```

**Forbidden:** writing a block, submitting (unless INPUT_SURFACE), moving a physics body, writing the camera or a viewport property (pipeline root only), reading `sanity.perception` (Filter and Debug only).

### Pipeline root and render layout [ADR-0008 § 3, § 6; PIPE PR-12, PR-20]

```gdscript
class_name PipelineRoot extends Node             # process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION; the single PresentationHost
func setup(clock: PresentationClock, driver: PresentationDriver, tuning: RenderTuning,
		settings: DisplaySettings, hud_layout: HudLayout) -> void
func request_zoom_step(direction: int) -> void   # +1 in, -1 out; edge-triggered; rate-limited

class_name RenderLayout extends RefCounted       # pure value; written only by PipelineRoot; handed out read-only
func world_to_hud(body_pos: Vector2i, pose_q: Vector2i) -> Vector2i          # the only projection to HUD coordinates; floored to the HUD grid
func mouse_to_world_aim(cursor_px: Vector2i, f_q: Vector2i) -> Vector2       # open loop (D.14b); the only mapping that feeds beam aim
func mouse_to_world_view(cursor_px: Vector2i, pose_q: Vector2i) -> Vector2   # picking and pings; never beam aim (lint, ADR-0010)
```

*(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0008 sync)* `PipelineRoot` is the only writer of viewport, container and layer geometry; the camera is solved in the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage and `frame_pre_draw` only writes `canvas_transform` and the parallax offsets. Subscribers receive `RenderLayout` read-only and re-derive nothing.

### Interface types still to define

The signatures above use types that no GDD defines field by field. Each is defined in the named ADR before the first story that implements it; programmers must not invent them.

| Type | Defined in |
|---|---|
| `Command`, `BlockDescriptor` (full field list), `CommandTypeDescriptor`, `ReadViews`, `WriteScope`, `ApplyContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `HookContext`, `NotifyContext`, `CompletionToken` (who constructs it; per call or pooled) | ADR-0003 |
| `ChangeBatch` (kernel-held PackedInt64Array behind key(i)/has(key)), `NotifyEvent`, `DirtyAccumulator`, `KeyBuf`, `KeySpaceDescriptor`, `SubscriptionHandle`, `NotifyFacet` (src/kernel/facets/ except KeySpaceDescriptor) | ADR-0004 (Proposed) |
| `FAULT_CODE` table: one closed enumeration per owning system, the kernel's own codes, and who may raise which | ADR-0003 |
| Per-command payload schemas and the payload validator | ADR-0002 (each command's owner lists its schema) |
| `QueryBuffer`, `SolidQuery`, `OccluderSource` | ADR-0014 |
| `JoinPlan`, `WeldResult`, `FailureFilter`, `FailureSlice` | ADR-0011, ADR-0012 |
| `LocoState`, `LocoIntent`, `LocoResult` | ADR-0015 |
| `PerceptionRef`, `Perceived`, `PerceptionTag` | ADR-0024 |

**How presentation reaches the kernel.** ADR-0001 (Proposed) decides it: no autoload and no `Kernel` global; the composition root hands each module the narrowest injected facet through `setup(facet)`. A simulation module gets a `ModuleFacet` (registrar, simulation views, fault domain, RNG facet and a read-only `ClockView`, ADR-0003); presentation gets a `PresentationFacet` (class-bound `subscribe`, `PresentationViews`, a read-only `PresentationClock` with `tick_alpha`, `T`, `running`, `state` and `load_seq`; ADR-0009 § 1), and per-frame alpha arrives as `frame.alpha` on the `PresentFrame`. Submit and control rights come only from the named handles of ADR-0002 (`SurfaceHandle`, `ControlHandle`). The examples in this document therefore use facets, not `Kernel.`; the remaining `Kernel.step()` and `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()` in the frame diagram are the `TickDriver`'s own calls on the kernel it was constructed with.

**How an interface is expressed.** GDScript has no interfaces. ADR-0010 (Proposed) picks `@abstract` ports for injected seams (probed on the 4.7.2 editor binary; fallback a plain base class whose methods `push_error`); kernel-invoked owner callables stay registered Callables (ADR-0003); duck-typed checking survives only as `ContractCheck` for recorded stubs. *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0010 sync)*

### Engine-type flags at the boundaries

| Type used in an interface | Version note | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `RefCounted` as block base (never `Resource`, never `Node`) | unchanged | LOW |
| `Callable` returning a typed `CompletionToken` | 4.7 typed-return override rule | HIGH, verify |
| `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedInt64Array` columns | 4.7 element writes skip setters | HIGH, explicit dirty marking |
| `@abstract class OccluderSource` and the other injected ports | 4.5 feature | HIGH; ADR-0010 chooses `@abstract` ports (probed on the 4.7.2 editor binary; release export checked by LINT-SPIKE-1); fallback: plain base class with a `push_error` stub |
| `Rect2i`, `Vector2i` in signatures (never in snapshots) | unchanged | LOW |
| `StringName` action names | unchanged | LOW |
| `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD` | 4.7 | HIGH |

---

## Architecture Principles

1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

# PURPOSE: Single source of truth for key architectural stances that all ADRs
# must agree on. Skills check this before writing new ADRs to detect conflicts
# at authoring time — before stories are created against contradictory decisions.

#     quoted: unquoted, the second colon makes the file invalid YAML.
#   - When a stance changes: update the entry, set revised: to today's date,

state_ownership:

    interface: "PresentationClock.tick_alpha (read-only float in [0, 1]; held at 1.0 while the kernel is not RUNNING); presentation-only, never a state block, never hashed or saved, never read by the simulation"

    referenced_by:

    added: 2026-10-28

    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0002-authority-model-and-command-pipeline.md
    referenced_by:

      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
  - pattern: peer_id_keyed_persistent_state
    status: active
    description: "Persistent per-player state and ownership are keyed by PlayerId; the peer id appears only in the ingress stamp and binding table half (a). Ownership is never derived from scene-tree node authority."
    why: "Peer ids change on reconnect and host change; a copied save or re-join must keep its characters."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0002-authority-model-and-command-pipeline.md
    added: 2026-10-28
  - pattern: write_outside_writescope_or_setter_dirty
    status: active
    description: "No block is written outside a kernel WriteScope (APPLY, PAUSED_APPLY, HOOK, INIT, RESTORE); every mutator begins with scope.open_for; dirty keys are marked only through scope.mark_dirty, never from a property setter."

# ADR-0007: Static Content Data Pipeline and Stable Type IDs

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/item-and-module-database.md` IDB-3, IDB-4, IDB-26, IDB-27, IDB-30; `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-2, LY-30; `life-support-graph.md` LS-2 to LS-5 and `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID`; `derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` DA-4, DA-41; `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md` rows citing ADR-0007; ADR-0003 § 6; and `docs/engine-reference/godot/` `VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md`, `deprecated-apis.md`). No code exists and nothing here has been run on 4.7.2. The pinned engine reference has no core, scripting or export module, so every engine claim about `FileAccess`, `JSON`, `DirAccess` and export filters rests on training knowledge of APIs that predate 4.4 and is spike-bound (CONTENT-EXP-1).

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under `modes.automation: autonomous` (`project.yaml`), with every decision point logged in `production/session-logs/decision-log.md` for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR. Reviewed by godot-specialist (engine: idiomatic; three blocking detail errors and fifteen minor notes, all applied) and technical-director (TD-ADR: CONCERNS; findings 1 to 12 applied in this revision). See Review Log.

## Summary
Sixty-five requirements from fifteen GDDs need static authored data (items, section templates, world records, tuning tables, lint configuration) to load identically in the editor, headless tests and a release export, to reach the simulation only as integers, and to keep ids stable across saves. This ADR fixes one pipeline: integer-only JSON under `assets/data/` listed in committed manifests (never a directory scan), read through an injected `ContentSource`, parsed with `JSON.new().parse`, cast through closed per-table schemas into write-once typed `RefCounted` catalogs, validated by one flat domain-2 boot-error list plus an offline lint that reuses the same loaders, and keyed by append-only id ledgers that CI diffs against a base revision.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (file I/O, JSON parsing, project export configuration, data-class design) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | LOW for the APIs (`FileAccess.open`, `FileAccess.get_open_error`, `FileAccess.get_as_text`, `JSON.new().parse`, `JSON.get_data` / `get_error_line` / `get_error_message`, `Array.make_read_only` / `is_read_only`, `roundi`, `Performance.get_monitor(OBJECT_COUNT)` all predate 4.4 and are not listed in `breaking-changes.md` for 4.4 to 4.7). MEDIUM confidence overall, because the pinned reference has no core/scripting/export module: JSON number typing, the include-filter glob syntax and the export of `.json` files are training-knowledge claims, bound to spike CONTENT-EXP-1. The 4.7 rows that matter are the typed-return override rule (every `ContentSource` override returns a `ContentRead` on all paths) and the packed-array element-write change (not engaged: catalogs have no setters). |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.4 `FileAccess.store_*` now return `bool`: irrelevant, runtime never writes content; 4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows), `deprecated-apis.md` (untyped Array/Dictionary pattern row), `current-best-practices.md` (not read for this ADR; its GDScript 4.5 to 4.7 rows are cited through ADR-0003). No module file exists for this domain. |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None required. Typed `Dictionary[K, V]` (4.4) may be used for key-indexed lookup maps. |
| **Verification Required** | **CONTENT-EXP-1 (gates acceptance).** On a `template_release` export for Windows **and for Linux / Steam Deck** (case-sensitive file system), with the preset filters in § 1.6, a headless boot reads every manifest-listed file with `FileAccess.open`, builds the same `ContentSet` as the editor, and yields identical content hashes (AC-178). Record: (a) whether `.json` files are exported raw via `include_filter` or as `JSON` resources through Godot's built-in JSON loader, and whether `FileAccess.open` on the original `res://` path works in both cases (both outcomes are recorded, since they decide whether `EXPORT_FILTER_MISSES_MANIFEST` is needed); (b) the `include_filter` / `exclude_filter` glob behaviour for nested paths (expected: comma-separated, `matchn`, `*` matches `/`); (c) that `JSON.new().parse` returns `float` for every number (`40000`, `40000.0`, `1e9

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | ADR-0001 (composition root injects; no autoload or global; Proposed), ADR-0003 (fault domain 2 and the `*_faults.gd` convention; Proposed). *(Amended 2026-10-28, cross-ADR ruling TD-27.)* |
| **Validation follow-up (not an acceptance prerequisite)** | ADR-0005 (golden content-hash vectors only, committed after ADR-0005 is Accepted, § Validation Criteria; Proposed). |
| **Enables** | ADR-0006 (Save/Load header carries `catalogue_version`; `block_versions.json` loads through this pipeline; TD-27), ADR-0011 (Graph data model: type tables loaded by this pipeline), ADR-0013 (Layout block: templates, ids and hashes), ADR-0017 (Emitter reads Failure & Trail's glow table as static content), ADR-0010 (lint tool enforces § 2 and § 3), ADR-0008 (the tuning loader for `RenderTuning`, a `ScalarTable` with a typed row table), and every Item DB, Layout template, Derelict Authoring, Horror, Sanity, Audio, Instruments, HUD and Chart Table data story. |
| **Blocks** | Epics: Item & Module Database, Ship Section & Layout (template loading), Derelict Authoring (lint and converter), and every story that adds a data file under `assets/data/`. |
| **Ordering Note** | **Forward references (not yet written, not blocking authorship):** ADR-0005 owns the canonical byte encoding and `H64`; this ADR fixes only the hash *input* (post-cast typed integers). ADR-0006 owns the save header; this ADR only defines and offers `catalogue_version`. ADR-0010 owns the source layout and the location of shared pure functions (§ 1.9). Acceptance requires ADR-0001 and ADR-0003 Accepted and CONTENT-EXP-1 passed. **Scope edge with ADR-0003:** content loads *before* the kernel exists (architecture § 8 steps 3 and 4), so content boot failures are handled by the composition root, not by the kernel's `boot_validation_failed` trigger (§ 2.3). This ADR uses ADR-0003's domain 2 exactly as that table defines it ("content data: item DB, templates, tuning"). |

## Context

### Problem Statement
Twenty-six GDDs make gameplay values, templates, catalogues and id spaces data-driven. Each GDD solved the same four problems locally and deferred the shared answer to this ADR: (1) the engine's JSON parser returns floats, but the simulation is integer-only; (2) a directory scan or an unlisted file can pass in the editor and fail or reorder in a release export; (3) a catalogue read by `validate`, P3 and presentation must be immutable, scene-tree free and allocation-free on lookup; (4) ids that reach a save, a snapshot or a hash must never change meaning. Without one decision, the Item DB, Layout, Graph, Derelict Authoring, Horror, Sanity and Audio would each ship a slightly different loader, and the first exported build would find the differences.

### Constraints
- **Integer-only simulation** (kernel, Graph LS-1, Layout LY-2). A float never reaches a sim read; designer floats convert once, at load.
- **No directory scan, no unordered iteration** (LY-2, IDB-4, LSG 64). The sim never iterates a `Dictionary`.
- **Same boot assertions in editor and export** (TR-sanity-026, AC-SN-178).
- **No autoload, static variable or group lookup** exposes content (registry `kernel_autoload_or_global`, ADR-0001); many catalogues coexist in one process (TR-itemdb-002).
- **Catalogs are never `Resource`** (registry `block_as_resource_or_node` extended by the same reasoning; SL-2; IDB-26 i).
- **No `assert`, no `push_error`, no `quit` in a loader** (`assert` is stripped in release; `push_error` trips gdUnit4; a loader that quits cannot be tested).
- **No `res://` path on any field that can reach a save** (IDB-26).
- **Unit tests do no file I/O** (coding standards): the loader needs a file-access seam.
- **Fault codes** follow ADR-0003 § 6: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, one `*_faults.gd` per domain, `NAMES` indexed by local code, append-only.
- **Dependency direction** (architecture "Which way dependencies may point"): Foundation code under `src/data/` must not import `src/sim/`; no `preload` of a sibling system's script.
- **Load budget:** `ItemCatalog` load plus freeze creates exactly 25 Objects and P99 <= 14.9 ms desktop / 30.0 ms Deck, pending spike (TR-itemdb-024).
- **Pre-release saves are disposable** (LSG 832); ids become binding at the first build given to anyone outside the project.

### Requirements
- One `ContentLoader` path for every static table, used unchanged by the game, gdUnit4 fixtures and the offline lint.
- A closed schema per table; unknown key, missing key, wrong type, float where an integer is required, and out-of-range value are errors with a stable code.

| GDD System | Requirement | How This ADR Addresses It |
|------------|-------------|--------------------------|
| item-and-module-database.md | TR-itemdb-001/002/003: static immutable `ItemCatalog` loaded once, injected, typed `RefCounted` defs, no static or autoload state | § 1.5 catalog pattern, § 1.8 injection |
| item-and-module-database.md | TR-itemdb-004/005/023: pure read-only queries, `defs_of_class` ascending `type_id`, no allocation | § 1.5 (sorted read-only arrays, `NO_DEF`); CONTENT-PERF-1 and § Validation identity checks |
| item-and-module-database.md | TR-itemdb-006/007/021/026: `def_id` persists, `type_id` in memory, `ids.lock.json` boot refusal, renames and retirement | § 3.1 to § 3.3 |
| item-and-module-database.md | TR-itemdb-008/009/010: integer-only JSON under `assets/data/items/`, boot order and closed failure list, port validation against LS-4 | § 1.1, § 1.4, § 1.7, § 2.3 |
| item-and-module-database.md | TR-itemdb-020: single `catalogue_version`, diagnostic `catalogue_hash` | § 3.4 |
| item-and-module-database.md | TR-itemdb-024: catalogue load creates exactly 25 Objects; load budget | § 1.5; CONTENT-PERF-1 (loader temporaries excluded) |
| life-support-graph.md | TR-lsg-030: type ids explicit, stable, unique-checked, append-only; Item DB then Layout then `graph.state` last | § 3.2 code-fixed tables, § 1.7 resolution |
| ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md | TR-section-003/029: templates immutable, loaded at start-up from a committed manifest in sorted order, int-cast and bound-checked, structural lint at load | § 1.2, § 1.4, § 2.1 BOOT tier, § 3.5 |
| derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md | TR-derelict-002/003/004/007/008: four template files, no new schema, integers only, hashes change on edit | § 1.1, § 1.4, § 3.5 |
| derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md | TR-derelict-013/016/023/024/025: BOOT rules incl. `PLACEMENT_DEF_UNKNOWN`, pure deterministic lint, tranches | § 2.1, § 2.2, § 2.4 |
| derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md | TR-derelict-027: plan-grammar converter is deterministic and a prerequisite | § 2.6 |
| web-map-and-transit.md | TR-webmap-006: roster and legs from `assets/data/world/`, linted on load | § 1.1, § 1.2, § 1.7 stage 4 |
| save-load-and-versioned-format.md | TR-saveload-024: boot asserts tuning-knob invariants against the data file | § 2.5 |
| player-controller-input.md | TR-pc-015: tick-expressed knobs invalidated by a `TICK_RATE` change, detected from the unit column | § 1.4 tick-expressed values |
## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: Boot only. Parse, cast and freeze run once per start on the main thread, before the kernel exists; nothing here runs in the tick. Lookups are an array index or a frozen-map lookup that allocates nothing (AC-69). Item catalogue load P99 <= 14.9 ms desktop / 30.0 ms Deck is the target, pending CONTENT-PERF-1; other tables get budgets from the same spike.
- **Memory**: Frozen rows only. The Item DB holds exactly 25 Objects (23 `ItemDef`, the `NO_DEF` sentinel, one `ItemCatalog`) once loader temporaries (`JSON`, `ContentRead`, `IntRead`, `FieldSpec`, `BootError`) are released, and returns to baseline when released. Raw text and parsed `Dictionary` trees are dropped after freeze.
- **Load Time**: Added to cold start. If CONTENT-PERF-1 shows a problem, stages 3 and 4 load behind a splash, never in the tick; no threaded load is planned, because it would add a synchronisation seam to a path that must be deterministic.
- **Network**: None. Content is not replicated; co-op peers load the same files and compare `catalogue_hash` / template hashes as a diagnostic.

## Migration Plan
No code exists. **GDD sync applied 2026-10-28** (each edit is marked *Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0007 sync* in its GDD). The copies of TR-lsg-030 and TR-section-003 in `tr-registry.yaml` and `requirements-traceability.md` are refreshed by `/architecture-review` Phase 8, which owns those files. The edits were:
- `item-and-module-database.md`:
  - IDB-26: close the export-filter and `catalogue_hash` ADR candidates; adopt the `BootError` shape and the Item DB manifest.
  - IDB-30: the composition root acts, not kernel BOOTING; codes are domain 2.
  - IDB-27: alias behaviour is a pre-`SHIPPED` story.
- `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-2 and LY-30: filter syntax; a template ledger; structural-lint codes are domain 2; "loaded in BOOTING" means start-up before the kernel.
- `life-support-graph.md`: the type-table baseline is the code enums; the `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID` code moves to domain 2 (`GRAPH_RESTORE_*` stays in domain 3).
- `sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md`: `SANITY_BOOT_LIE_TARGET_DATA` is domain 2.
- `suit-and-equipment.md`: ADR candidate 2 is closed (JSON).
- `failure-and-trail-system.md` and `emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query.md`: IC-12 wording.
- `architecture.md`:
  - § 8: static type tables load first; `graph.state` registers last.
  - Add CONTENT-EXP-1 to § Spikes that gate ADRs.
- `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md`: rewording of TR-lsg-030 and TR-section-003 ("loaded in BOOTING"). Re-tagging of the owner-elsewhere rows above happens at `/architecture-review`.

## Validation Criteria
- CONTENT-EXP-1 passes on Windows and Linux/Deck: an exported `template_release` boots headless to `RUNNING` and its content hashes equal the editor's.
- A unit test per loader rule: each pipeline-generic code is raised by a `MemoryContentSource` fixture with exactly one defect; a defect-free fixture loads clean; a fixture with defects in two files of one stage reports both.
- Two `ItemCatalog` instances built in one process share no state.
- **Zero allocation is tested two ways**, because `OBJECT_COUNT` counts only Objects and misses arrays:
  - (a) `OBJECT_COUNT` is unchanged over 10,000 queries;
  - (b) two calls to each array-returning accessor return the same array (`is_same`), and `is_read_only()` is true.
- The 25-Object load check runs after every loader temporary is out of scope.
- A CI job fails on:
  - an unlisted `.json`;
  - a case mismatch;
  - an include-filter miss;
  - a raw-text shape or duplicate-key violation;
  - a non-append-only ledger change or a missing `catalogue_version` bump after `SHIPPED`;
  - a generated file that drifts from its generator;
  - any `DirAccess`, `FileAccess`, `JSON.parse_string` or `JSON.new` use for content outside `src/data/` (the lint is ADR-0010's).
- **After ADR-0005 is Accepted** (a validation follow-up, not an acceptance prerequisite of this ADR): golden `catalogue_hash` and per-template hash vectors are committed and change only with the encoding.

## Related
- Depends on: ADR-0001, ADR-0003 (both Proposed).
- Forward references: ADR-0005 (canonical encoding, `H64`), ADR-0006 (save header carries `catalogue_version`), ADR-0010 (lint tool, source layout, shared pure functions), ADR-0011 (Graph type enums), ADR-0013 (layout block), ADR-0016 (restore ordering), ADR-0030 (boot-failure surface styling).
- GDDs: `item-and-module-database.md` (IDB-3, 4, 26, 27, 30), `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` (LY-2, LY-30), `life-support-graph.md` (LS-2 to LS-5, ADR-LSG-08), `derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` (DA-4, DA-41, DA-43), `save-load-and-versioned-format.md`.
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` § 8, § Required ADRs, § Spikes that gate ADRs, Open Question OQ-9.
- `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`: entries proposed by this ADR (state, interface, API decisions, forbidden patterns).

## Open Questions
- **OQ-A.** The composition root alone acts on content boot errors (content precedes the kernel), and domain 2 is not registered with the kernel at MVP. Revisit with ADR-0003 if the kernel GDD's boot-failure screen must be kernel-owned, or if a runtime path starts raising domain-2 codes.
- **OQ-B.** Whether the `section_templates` ledger holds one entry per `room_key` or one per template with a nested list (ADR-LAY-04 detail). This ADR requires the ledger and leaves the nesting to Layout's schema.
- **OQ-C (2026-10-29).** May a named structural invariant (§ 2.5) read a value from another table? The Suit GDD's SUIT_A1, SUIT_A11 and SUIT_A15 compare Suit values with `W_MIN_WARNING_S`, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` and leg-run data owned elsewhere. Proposed answer for the owner: yes, only for a table loaded in an earlier stage of § 1.7, read through the loader's result by key, never copied; otherwise the check moves to the consuming system's post-load assertion. Decide before ADR-0007 is Accepted.

## Review Log
- **2026-10-28 godot-specialist (engine).** Idiomatic for 4.7.2; no removed or deprecated API.
  - Blocking, all applied:
    - B1: `const Array[FieldSpec]` does not compile; now `const` literal rows plus `static func fields()`.
    - B2: packed arrays are passed by reference and cannot be read-only; now typed read-only `Array[T]` or index accessors.
    - B3: `OBJECT_COUNT` misses arrays; identity and `is_read_only` checks added.
  - Minor, applied:
    - `set` renamed to `content`.
    - The `get_file_as_string` rationale is corrected.

# Godot Input — Quick Reference

Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.7 changes); 2026-02-12 (rest) | Engine: Godot 4.7

## What Changed Since ~4.3 (LLM Cutoff)

### 4.7 Changes
- **Mouse and keyboard device IDs**: `InputEvent.device` is
  `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD` (was `0`, which some
  joypads also use). Identify events by type, not `device == 0` (4.7 migration guide: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html)
- **`VirtualJoystick` node**: on-screen joystick with Fixed, Dynamic and
  Following modes
- **Gamepad gyro and accelerometer** readings are available (4.7 release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/)

### 4.6 Changes
- **Dual-focus system**: Mouse/touch focus is now separate from keyboard/gamepad focus
  - Visual feedback differs by input method
  - Custom focus implementations may need updating
- **Select Mode keybind changed**: "Select Mode" is now `v` key; old mode renamed "Transform Mode" (`q` key)

### 4.5 Changes
- **SDL3 gamepad driver**: Gamepad handling delegated to SDL library for better cross-platform support
- **Recursive Control disable**: Single property disables mouse/focus for entire node hierarchies

### 4.3 Changes (in training data)
- **InputEventShortcut**: Dedicated event type for menu shortcuts (optional)

## Current API Patterns

### Input Actions (unchanged)
```gdscript
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    var input_dir: Vector2 = Input.get_vector(
        &"move_left", &"move_right", &"move_forward", &"move_back"
    )
    if Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"jump"):
        jump()
```

### Input Events (unchanged)
```gdscript
func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
    if event is InputEventMouseButton:
        if event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT and event.pressed:
            handle_click(event.position)
    elif event is InputEventKey:
        if event.keycode == KEY_ESCAPE and event.pressed:
            toggle_pause()
```

### Focus Management (4.6 — CHANGED)
```gdscript
# Mouse/touch and keyboard/gamepad focus are now SEPARATE
# Visual styles may differ depending on which input method is active
# If you have custom focus drawing, test with both input methods

# Standard approach still works:
func _ready() -> void:
    %StartButton.grab_focus()  # Keyboard/gamepad focus

# But be aware: mouse hover focus != keyboard focus in 4.6
```

### Gamepad (4.5+ — SDL3 backend)
```gdscript
# API unchanged, but SDL3 provides:
# - Better device detection across platforms
# - Improved rumble support
# - More consistent button mapping

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
    if event is InputEventJoypadButton:
        if event.button_index == JOY_BUTTON_A and event.pressed:
            confirm_selection()
```

## Common Mistakes
- Not testing both mouse and keyboard focus paths (dual-focus in 4.6)
- Assuming `grab_focus()` affects mouse focus (it only affects keyboard/gamepad in 4.6)
- Using string literals instead of `StringName` (`&"action"`) for action names in hot paths

# Player Controller & Input

> Authoring guidance: .claude/docs/templates/guidance/game-design-document-guide.md (load per-section as you author — do not read entirely).

> **Status**: Designed
> **Author**: user + game-designer, ux-designer, gameplay-programmer, creative-director, systems-designer, qa-lead (via /design-system, autonomous)
> **Last Updated**: 2026-10-27 (re-review: 5 blocking findings and the recommended items applied, see the *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review* tags and Open Questions 29–31; earlier the same day, design review: 5 blocking findings and 14 recommended items applied; see the *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review* tags and Open Questions 16, 19–27; then the user's design-review rulings were applied, see the *Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings* tags and the resolved Open Questions 17, 19, 20, 21 and 26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
> **Re-review (2026-10-27)**: the five blocking findings and the recommended items of the re-review were applied; see the *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review* tags and Open Questions 29–31. The pipeline GDD's published `f_q` is kept (delegated ruling R4); the Controller-side run look-ahead weight is withdrawn in favour of the pipeline's (general rule G1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
> **Cross-GDD pass (2026-10-28)**: delegated rulings G6, R12, R14, R18 and the HUD K43 CD ruling applied: `channel_body` and the step-1 body edge (body-transfer channel clear, AC-PCI-223/224); DEAD hand-off timed after Save/Load's epoch staging; `ACTOR_SELF` and `give_up`-plate siblings marked conformed; `confirm_view` gains `mode`, `armed`, `give_up_live`; door `set_opening` carry-admitted; ignored-input dim and first-use captions removed; reference machines named. See the *Amended 2026-10-28* tags. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
> **Cross-GDD blocker pass, second round (2026-10-28)**: routed requests applied — `actor_source` on the intents and action commands; the camera shift `S` (`|S|` ≤ 36 px) mirroring pipeline D.14b; `face_octant` NONE, `octant_of` and the `channel_face = none` hold; the PC-6 self-target rule (`SELF_FOCUS_SCORE`, invariant 19); the BURDEN push and `salvage_carry`; the MenuInput stream (PC-2a); the per-verb hold cap `cap_v`. New ACs AC-PCI-076b, 105b–105d, 115b–115e, 225–230; Open Question 32. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
> **Last Verified**: 2026-10-26
> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: APPROVED 2026-10-26 (after one CONCERNS round: six documentation carry-through items for the chest-mounted lamp and the throw binding; no design change)
> **User rulings (design-review decisions)**: 2026-10-27 — the user ruled "I agree with all of your recommendations on those decisions, please fill them in accordingly" and then "yes to all" on the held items. Applied here: D6 (camera look-ahead weighted toward movement while running), D7 (solo "give up and reload" action while DOWNED), D8 (`FOLLOW_MOVE_WHEN_RELEASED` is the default), D9 (opt-in, off-by-default aim indicator), D10 (fixed reference chest `AIM_ORIGIN` confirmed), D94 (movement closes the inspect card and moves the avatar in the same frame), D18 (any stowed HEAVY item disables run), D60 (a death in the pod is the Controller's `DEAD`), X2 (no `pod_hop` lit waiver), X5 (`top_up` is an MVP verb), X10 (accessibility tier standard; hold-to-confirm two-tap and adjustable hold). D80 and D81 are applied as defaults confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20). X14 (reference machine) is closed by delegated ruling R12: RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, release export (Performance budget). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*
> **Implements Pillar**: Dread Before Chaos (P2 — the body's steadiness is what lets the two rhythms be read off the world instead of the controls); The Web Watches (P3 — every step, light and tool use is a stimulus the player owns); The World Never Lies (P1 — the body and its beam are never-shift anchors)

## Summary

The Player Controller & Input is the crewmate's body and hands: it turns keyboard, mouse or gamepad input into the two things the simulation accepts — intents (where I am walking, where my chest lamp points, whether I am running) and commands (cut, weld, pick up, drop, throw a glowstick) — and turns the simulation's answer back into a stiff, heavy, honest body on screen. The body is the same in the quiet boarding rhythm and the frantic breach: no adrenaline, no speed change, nothing that lets a player read the danger off their controls instead of off the world. Movement is whole-pixel integer kinematics with no physics body; the lamp is chest-mounted and hands-free; every acknowledgement is immediate and never encodes success; the sprite, its tools and its beam are anchors a hallucination can never edit. Sixteen systems depend on the intent/command split and the facing, reach and noise rules it fixes.

> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Core` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer`, `Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera` (both designed); position ownership adopted with `Ship Body & Interior Physics` (PC-14; technical-director ratification pending) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

## Overview

The Player Controller & Input is the crewmate's body and hands: it turns what the player does at the keyboard, mouse or gamepad into the two kinds of thing the simulation accepts — **intents** (where I am trying to walk, where I am pointing the beam, whether I am running) and **commands** (cut this hatch, toggle the beam, pick that up, drop it, start welding) — and it turns the simulation's answer back into a body on screen: five drawn facings and their mirrors, a stiff-weighted walk and run, a module carried at chest height, a stagger when the air goes bad, the lamp beam from the suit's chest-mounted light at the per-facing chest point. In the simulation it owns the player's intent and facing as a `PER_PLAYER` state block keyed by seat; whether it also owns ship-local position, or Ship Body & Interior Physics does, is the one open boundary it shares with that system (kernel Open Question 3) and is settled in this GDD provisionally.

The player operates this system every second of play, and its whole design goal is that they stop noticing it. It is active in the deliberate boarding rhythm (every step a decision, the beam swept slowly onto a doorway) and in the frantic breach rhythm (running a corridor while the ship fails around them) — and it is **the same body in both**: no adrenaline, no speed buff, no change of handling. The breach is frantic because of what moves in the world, not because the body changes (art bible 2.8).

It exists because the pillars put the player's body on the truth side of the game. *The World Never Lies*: the character sprite, its tools and its beam are never-shift anchors — a crewmate rendered as a horror still carries their true beam, and the body's honest states (rime, fogged visor, stagger) are a cross-check a low-sanity player can trust. *The Web Watches*: every step, every lit beam and every running stride is a stimulus the player owns — running is loud, and the controller is where that cost is paid. *Dread Before Chaos*: a slow, heavy body makes a door a decision. Every downstream system that needs a player to act — Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Modular Ship Assembly, Attention, the camera's follow target, the HUD's hand rail, co-op bodies as mirrored state — depends on the intent/command split this GDD fixes.

**Design-level only.** `CharacterBody2D` vs hand-rolled kinematics on a moving ship, how input actions are read, the animation driver — implementation choices → **becomes an ADR** (ship body / interior physics; input adapter). *(Framing: both the data layer and its player impact — `Core` category says technical, but this is the system the player is; fantasy direct.)*

**PC-1. Three parts, and the control-manifest lines that separate them.** (a) The **Input Adapter** reads devices, quantises, and submits `PLAYER`-origin commands as peer 1 acting on the entity the binding table binds to PlayerId 1 (CR-7). It writes no block, ever; it owns only local state (raw aim, last-acknowledged intents, hold timers, run latch, active device, context, pre-play tokens, menu latch and last NAV direction). It samples input for gameplay intents **in its own `_process`, at a process priority below the TickDriver node's, so before the driver's boundary service and tick loop** (ADR-0001 § 3; the MenuInput stream of PC-2a is sampled on render frames) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0001 GDD sync)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)*, so an intent submitted in frame N is frozen into tick T's P1 batch, applied in P2 and integrated by Body in P3 of the same tick — one tick of latency, never two. It never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` read view: input mapping, dead-zones and aim source are HR-6 anchors and must be structurally unable to lie. (b) The **Controller Sim** registers `controller.state` (`SIM`, `persist = true`, `persist_scope = WORLD`, `scope = PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId, `repl_hint = SHARED_SUMMARY`), command types `set_move_intent` and `set_aim`, the `PLAYER`-origin command **`give_up {actor}`** (`coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`; validate: `loco_state == DOWNED` and no other bound seat that could revive (solo, MVP), else rejected `NOT_DOWNED`; apply: `death_tick := min(death_tick, T)`, so the existing D.14 check order does the rest in the same tick's `controller.step`: cap first, then death; PC-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D7, the solo "give up and reload" action)*, and hook `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`). It writes its block in its own `apply` handlers, inside its hooks, and through four published **Class B mutators** that other owners' `apply` handlers and hooks call for cross-block writes (CR-9 a): `set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant)`, `clear_channel_ref(actor)`, `set_carry_ref(actor, item_id)`, `clear_carry_ref(actor)` (Interaction IA-36; Modular Ship Assembly calls `set_channel_ref(actor, ASSEMBLY, channel_id, face_octant)` and `clear_carry_ref(actor)`; `face_octant` is the owner's `octant_of(target anchor − foot)` computed at the `begin_*` apply and stored as `controller.state.channel_face`, so the facing lock of PC-4 rule 2 reads stored data that a MIRROR client has and never recomputes) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `face_octant` added; the mutators are not kernel-invoked callables, they take the shared `WriteScope`, report with `scope.fault` and return a status that callers propagate, while every Controller callable the kernel invokes — `validate`, `apply`, `controller.step`, `controller.noise`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `read_view` — receives `ctx` and ends in `return ctx.complete()`, kernel CR-19, delegated ruling R3)*; it may not submit `PLAYER`-origin commands (CR-3). `face_octant` ∈ {0..7, NONE}, NONE being 8, the same sentinel as `octant`. The owner passes NONE (1) for object class `ACTOR_SELF` (the self-patch has no target anchor) and (2) when `anchor_o − foot` = (0, 0); `anchor_o` is the target subject's interaction anchor (D.9) and `foot` is the actor's `pos_curr`, both in the actor's body frame, the same pair `in_reach` uses, and the octant is `octant_of` (D.8). A value outside 0..8 is `scope.fault` with a non-OK status and writes nothing. Callers: Interaction's `begin_*` applies (IA-14) and Assembly's `begin_weld` / `begin_seam_cut` applies (MSA-30). The four mutators are published here and the siblings conform. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))* It also registers the `SYSTEM`-origin command type **`stagger {actor}`** (`allowed_origins {SYSTEM}`, `coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`, no player binding; rejected `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD`; `Applied` in `STAGGERED` without extending the lock, so a stagger never chains into a stun-lock), which Suit & Equipment submits on a two-band pressure drop within `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` (SE-35) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment)* (Horror Entities submits none, HE-6; PC-9), and a second divisor-1 hook **`controller.noise`** (`after: [body.integrate]`, D.13). Its `SIM` read view publishes `octant`, `run`, `gait_effective`, `aim_angle`, `aim_live`, `facing`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, `salvage_carry` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP; user ruling X3, delegated ruling R5)*, `channel_ref`, the chest point and the hand point; `loco_state` is the name Attention (AT-31: the living-player and `IN_POD` tests) and Horror (HE-33, C-HE-18) read. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, modular-ship-assembly, suit-and-equipment, ship-body-and-interior-physics, attention-system, horror-entities)* (c) The **Avatar Presenter** reads `body.state` (integer position prev/curr, odometer), `controller.state` (facing, gait, locomotion state, chest point, hand point), `emitter.state` (beam lit, shape) and `tick_alpha`; for the *local* avatar only it also reads the Adapter's raw aim. It writes exactly: frame index, `flip_h`, integer position, overlay visibility, light position and light rotation — **never scale, rotation, skew or modulate on the body** (lint). *Rationale.* "Controller submits via `INPUT_SURFACE` only; never writes blocks" is true of the Adapter and false of the Controller Sim; one name for both would read as "this system has no block", and facing and gait would end up as presentation state that co-op cannot replicate and a save cannot restore. *Alternative rejected:* folding the Controller Sim into Ship Body — intent and facing are seat semantics (what the player asked for, read by Interaction, Attention and the HUD); position is a kinematic fact. Keeping them apart keeps the input record separate from the integrator.

**PC-2. Input model: contexts, actions, intents, commands.** The game reads **named actions** (`StringName`, rebindable), never raw keys and never `device == 0` (4.7: `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`; identify devices by event type). **→ ADR** (InputMap vs a custom binding layer; edge detection by event vs polling).

*Contexts.* Exactly one context is active: `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`. Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch; entering `chart_table` or `chat` also submits `cancel_channel` for a hold- **or** toggle-mode channel (in the co-op overlay the sim keeps running and a channel the player cannot see must not keep burning); entering `inspect_card` does **not** cancel the channel, so the Pillar 4 "second instrument" check on the pipe being welded is free (the zeroed move intent is not a move, the channel continues, `interact` is still tracked for hold mode and a release inside the card still cancels; `cancel` closes the card first and a second `cancel` cancels the channel). **Movement closes the card** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D94, the Controller's context-matrix amendment adopted; the In-World Instruments fallback "buffer and replay the first move press" is void)*: a **fresh** movement input in `inspect_card` (a `move_*` key going down, or the left stick crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`) returns the context to `gameplay` **and** submits `set_move_intent` for that octant in the same frame, in that order, so the first press both closes the card and moves the avatar (nothing is swallowed, nothing is buffered). A direction already held when the card opened is latched and does not count until it is released (or the stick falls below the exit band) and pressed again, so opening the card while walking does not close it on the next frame. A move that closes the card while a channel is running is an ordinary non-`NONE` move intent and aborts the channel exactly as it does in `gameplay`. Any transition of `loco_state` to `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD` returns the context to `gameplay` on the same frame (the Adapter observes the published state; the card or overlay closes and the cursor is hidden again). Pause is reachable in every state including `DOWNED`: `chart_table` and `request_pause` are Adapter-level and never gated by `loco_state`. **PC-2a. MenuInput stream (Adapter-owned; consumer: the Chart Table layer, CT-45).** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)* The Adapter publishes a presentation-local MenuInput event stream while the active context is `chart_table`; before a campaign is loaded (the boot-flow screens) the Adapter runs in the `chart_table` context with no gameplay sink and publishes the same stream. It is sampled on render frames (the gameplay-intent sampling of PC-1 (a) happens in the Adapter's `_process` just before the TickDriver and serves gameplay intents only); all events of one render frame are delivered in arrival order at the start of that frame, before the layer's update. **Events:** `NAV_DOWN{dir, source}` and `NAV_UP{dir}` (`dir` ∈ {UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT}; `source` ∈ {STICK, DPAD, ARROW, WASD}); `ACCEPT_DOWN`, `ACCEPT_UP`; `BACK`; `CLOSE`; `FOCUS_OUT`, `FOCUS_IN`; `DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`; `POINTER{kind ∈ {MOVE, DOWN, UP, WHEEL}, button, position}`, where `position` is the cursor in physical window px, forwarded unconverted (the root viewport mouse position; root stretch is disabled, ADR-0008 § 5); the Chart Table layer subtracts `RenderLayout.picture_rect.position` itself, and the Controller's aim path (PC-5) subtracts the world picture's origin exactly once, so each consumer subtracts once and the Adapter's stream value is never subtracted twice; the unit is settled, not **[UNV]** (AC-CT-135 (f) only confirms it) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0008 sync)*. **The Adapter owns:** (a) **echo suppression**: an OS key echo of a held E, Enter, Space, Esc or X produces no second event (the engine's echo flag is **[UNV]** until the ADR spike); (b) **deadzone hysteresis**: a stick takes a NAV edge on crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` and releases below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, the same band as the `inspect_card` movement rule (PC-2 contexts); (c) **the cardinal-axis rule**: a stick yields one NAV direction at a time, the axis with the larger magnitude, a tie going to the vertical axis; the taken direction changes only after the stick has re-passed the exit band, so a diagonal drift cannot alternate; auto-repeat of a held NAV direction is the layer's (Chart Table D.9); (d) **latch-until-released**: for any physical control whose press closed the layer (Resume accept, `chart_table`, `cancel`) the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it is physically released and pressed again, including across the `PAUSED → RUNNING` resync (Edge Cases, kernel `PAUSED`); for a console press that opened the layer, the open press's release and repeats are latched the same way; (e) **focus**: `FOCUS_OUT` releases every held menu control and clears navigation state, and the layer's hold fills abort; on `FOCUS_IN` nothing is held and fresh presses are required; (f) **`DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`** is published when the last-used-device glyph set changes under PC-13 (immediately, except inside `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS` of the previous change, when it is published at the window end), so the layer adds no delay; (g) **the cursor hint**: the layer publishes `cursor_hint` ∈ {DEFAULT, SELECTABLE}; the Adapter, its only `Input` caller, applies the pointer-cursor shape. The `zoom_*` edges are never emitted in this context (PC-16). The stream carries no gameplay command and no simulation read. Its code lives in the Adapter's registered files (AC-PCI-176).

*Dev-only actions (dev feature tag only).* The Adapter registers the ten actions of registry `debug_overlay_actions` — `debug_overlay_toggle`, `debug_overlay_page_next`, `debug_overlay_page_prev`, `debug_overlay_mode`, `debug_overlay_dump`, `debug_overlay_reveal`, `debug_overlay_mark`, `debug_overlay_cursor_next`, `debug_overlay_cursor_prev`, `debug_overlay_activate` (placeholder defaults toggle F3, page next F4, page prev Shift+F4, mode Insert, dump Home, reveal Ctrl+Shift+F3 with the pad chord L3 + R3, mark End, cursor next PageDown, cursor prev PageUp, activate Delete; F5-F8 avoided as editor run, pause and stop shortcuts; Debug Overlay DO-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* — **only under the dev feature tag**, and forwards them host-locally to the Overlay: never a command, never in the binding table Settings sees, never in a rebinding, preset or accessibility enumeration, absent from release. The Adapter is their only `Input` reader (Gaps: the cross-GDD lint collision). **Pad chord:** the dev chord L3 + R3 shadows no gameplay action now that `throw` is on RB; L3 and R3 are unbound by default in every build. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from debug-overlay-true-values; rewritten 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "R3 consumed by the chord before `throw`" rule is void)*

*Intents vs commands (CR-4).* Two types are **intents**, `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`, `max_age_ticks = 30`: **`set_move_intent {octant: 0..7 | 8 = NONE, run: bool}`** and **`set_aim {aim_angle: int, live: bool}`** in **1/4096-turn units** (`live` is `aim_live`: it travels with the angle because facing rules 4–6 branch on it in the sim). Both intents carry `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` with `actor_source = body.state` (the avatar's Body `actor_id`, kernel CR-7), like commands. Everything else is a **command**: `coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`, `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` as its owner declares (`body.state` for every avatar-acting verb; `emitter.state` for `toggle_beam`, whose `actor` is the seat's beam id) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The Adapter sends `set_move_intent` **only on change** of octant or `run`, with the stick quantised to 8 octants under `MOVE_DEADZONE` = 0.25 and `OCTANT_HYSTERESIS_DEG` = 5°. In one frame it submits `set_move_intent` **before** any command (submission order is the P2 apply order — the kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source) from it, and callers never choose it, delegated ruling R2 — so a stop and a `begin_*` in the same frame apply in that order, PC-7). It sends `set_aim` when the quantised value differs from `last_acked` by **≥ 1/128 turn (2.8°)**, **or** the aim source changed (mouse ↔ stick ↔ keys), **or** `live` changed, **or** a settle condition holds (inside the threshold but differing at all, for `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` = 6) — **rate-limited to one per `AIM_SEND_INTERVAL` = 3 ticks**. At rest that is zero sends; a sweep is ≤ 20 sends/s, far inside `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`. **No input buffering**: `ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS` = 0; a press during a channel is submitted and answered `BUSY`, honestly; nothing is queued for "after". *Rationale:* buffering hides the sim's answer behind a presentation guess; Zomboid's immediacy is the model. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Zero buffering is a recorded, deliberate trade, not an oversight:** an `interact` for a `CHANNEL` verb pressed one to three ticks before the move keys are up is rejected `MOVING` (PC-7) and costs one honest re-press; the same-tick case (release W and press E in one frame) is solved by ordering, not by buffering (intents are submitted first and validation reads `intent_octant`, PC-7). Adapter-side lever, **off at MVP**: `CHANNEL_BEGIN_GRACE_TICKS` (0–3, default **0**) would hold a `begin_*` press until the Adapter's own last-submitted octant is NONE for at most that many ticks; a playtest finding of "my weld never starts" is the trigger to raise it. *Ignored-input cues (accessibility):* four presses are dropped by Adapter-local knowledge alone and play one short dull cue (`cue_input_ignored`, the same id for all four, no visual, never read from a sim result): `toggle_beam` inside the rate-limit window (PC-5), `interact` with no focused object, `run` while `carry_ref ≠ none`, and `run` while the player's own inventory view shows a HEAVY item stowed (`stowed_heavy`, user ruling D18 and D.4; the name is the one Suit & Equipment publishes, registry `stowed_heavy`, and the earlier `heavy_stowed` is retired *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, general rule G1)*; it is the consequence of the player's own stow command, not a hidden reading) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D18)*. The cue is Adapter-local and so cannot reveal a sim answer; `run` under Suit's cap gets none (the cap is Suit's state, shown by the breath and warmth readings).

*Immediate acknowledgement and the pre-play token (CR-4).* On submit the Adapter pre-plays **body and sound only, never the effect**: the hand's switch animation, the tool click, the bar starting. Each pre-play is keyed by an opaque integer **`correlation`** the Adapter attaches to the command (a per-Adapter counter; the kernel echoes it unchanged in the result or rejection event; `submit()` stays void and fire-and-forget, and the kernel, not the caller, stamps `seq`) in a `correlation → pre-play token` map, so a late result cancels the right pre-play *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*. The beam light is the one object that is not pre-played (PC-5). **Rejection classes** (declared by each verb's owner, Interaction's GDD): *immediate* reasons — `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BUSY`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `PAUSED`, every admission reason — **withdraw the ack at once** (the sound stops, the bar vanishes within one frame of the result); the free-lie-detector case of Pillar 4 (a device the player perceives as broken or fixed) is **not a rejection**: the command is `Applied` and the channel resolves to a `PRECONDITION` outcome (Interaction, KRN:96), so the ack is never withdrawn — the work loop and the bar continue until Interaction's channel state signals the outcome. **The ack frame for a command whose channel will complete and one whose channel will resolve to `PRECONDITION` must be pixel- and sound-identical.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system)* Rejection is never a shake (C9, HR-13).

*Non-audio counterpart (HUD-owned; reduced to the MOVING tell).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated CD ruling, HUD re-review K43)* Every negative cue was audio-only, so deaf and hard-of-hearing players got none, and nothing taught the three core rules (channels need stillness, prompts need light, destructive verbs need a hold). The only non-audio counterpart at MVP is the pre-press tell for a `begin_*` press that the actor's **own** state would block (`MOVING`): Interaction's `focus_view.press_blocked_moving`, drawn by HUD as a hollow keycap on `CHANNEL` and `HOLD_CONFIRM` plates (Interaction IA-41, AC-IA-142). The Adapter publishes **no** `input_ignored_view(seat)` and no reason class to the HUD: a visible response to a `NOT_LIT` (or any subject-dependent) press would tell the player something is at the unlit subject, the unlit-subject oracle Pillar 3 forbids, so the glyph dim on `NOT_LIT`, `BUSY`-by-other-seat, `OUT_OF_RANGE` and `INVALID_TARGET` presses is refused; the HUD still holds the restored keycap for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` on a plate Interaction has already shown (HUD HS-41). The other ignored-input cues (`cue_input_ignored`: `toggle_beam` in its window, `interact` with no focus, `run` while carrying) stay audio-only at MVP; a non-audio counterpart for them is deferred to `design/accessibility-requirements.md` (Open Question 26) and must not key on subject existence or lighting. **First-use hints are refused**: no caption, no Settings "seen" flag, no "reset profile" interaction (HUD HS-57, anti-pillar 4; teaching belongs to the world, Cryo Bay onboarding). **Playtest metric:** ≥ 80 % of first-time testers complete the first weld within two attempts; a miss reopens the Cryo Bay onboarding (HUD OQ-HS-29), not the rules and not a HUD hint.

*Resync rule (one rule, five triggers).* The Adapter keeps `last_acked` per intent type and must **resend its current quantised value, bypassing the change filter once**, when: (i) an intent result arrives `Rejected(STALE)` (kernel Edge Cases: a stale "stop" otherwise leaves the actor moving); (ii) the kernel leaves `PAUSED` (CR-16 rejects intents immediately while paused, so a release during a pause was lost); (iii) `LOADING → RUNNING`; (iv) window focus returns, or the active gamepad reconnects; (v) **`TRANSFER`**: the actor's `body_of_actor` changes, i.e. a pod arrival (`IN_POD →` the locomotion-class member) or a section-detach body transfer, because the new body's first tick must act on the keys physically held *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: pod arrival and body transfer were handled only as an ad-hoc "treated as trigger iii" in Edge Cases)*. For a hold-mode channel it compares the actual button state to the last submitted one on each of those and submits `cancel_channel` if the button is up. **Window focus loss** submits `set_move_intent {NONE}` and `cancel_channel` if channelling, and marks every held action released; **the loss of the active gamepad** (a disconnect, mid-weld included) is treated identically (the same zero intent and cancel, the held pad actions released, the keyboard and mouse stay live, and a reconnect resyncs under trigger iv), and **the click or key press that returns window focus is consumed by the Adapter** and never reaches a binding (an LMB alias of `interact` would otherwise fire on refocus) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Invariant (testable): the sim's intent equals the player's hands within one tick of the kernel being `RUNNING`.

**PC-4. Facing: five drawn, three mirrored; derived from committed aim when the aim is live.** Facing is recomputed **every tick from committed state, with no easing, mid-cycle**, using a **2-quanta sector hysteresis** (2 × 1/128 turn = 5.6°) at octant boundaries. Priority order:
1. **Staggered / downed / dead**: facing frozen.
----
**PC-5. Aim and the beam.** *Sources.* Mouse: raw aim = direction from the **aim origin** `AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos_curr) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y)` (a fixed reference chest height, independent of facing, sheet and animation row; default `AIM_ORIGIN_Y` = −35) to the cursor's **look-ahead-free world point** `cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp − picture_centre) / k_eff`, where `f_q` is the pipeline's **published** follow pose **before** look-ahead, the inner-box clamp and jolt (pipeline D.6's `f`, floored to the camera quantum; pipeline D.14b publishes it every frame), `cursor_vp` the cursor in **physical window px** relative to the world picture's origin, `picture_centre = (L_w, L_h) · k_z / 2` in the same unit and `k_eff = k_z` the physical px per base px (the unit is the pipeline's D.14b `cursor_px`; the root viewport mouse position is already physical window px because root stretch is disabled (ADR-0008 § 5), so the Adapter reads it with no inverse stretch transform; the pipeline's in-engine acceptance criterion in "Camera follow, look-ahead, cuts" only confirms it) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0008 sync)*. **Who subtracts the letterbox offset:** the raw window-px value is *not* picture-relative; the Adapter's aim path forms `cursor_vp = cursor_window_px − RenderLayout.world_rect.position` (the world picture's top-left, D.14b `picture_origin`; it equals `picture_rect.position` whenever the world fills the picture, as at the default step) exactly once, then applies `(cursor_vp − picture_centre) / k_eff`. If it instead calls `RenderLayout.mouse_to_world_aim(cursor_px, f_q)` with the raw window px, that method performs the same single subtraction (D.14b `c_pic = cursor_px − picture_origin`) and the Adapter subtracts nothing. Never both; the Chart Table layer's own `picture_rect.position` subtraction (PC-2a) is a separate path that never feeds aim. With a non-zero letterbox, skipping the subtraction offsets the beam by `offset / k_eff` base px, so AC-PCI-056 and AC-PCI-059 use a letterboxed window *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix: ADR-0008 § 3.3, § 5; the Adapter-forwarded raw value left the picture-origin subtraction unowned)*; inside `AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX` = 8 base px of the aim origin the aim holds, **measured in picture space with the camera settled** (the near-body fixtures in Acceptance Criteria are authored that way; while the follow lag is non-zero the cursor-to-origin distance carries the lag term below). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R4: the Controller's form is canonical and the pipeline publishes `f_q`, a contract, no longer a request; the review's alternative of anchoring on the avatar `p = floor(pos_curr)` was not adopted, see the trade-off below)* **Why not C11's `cursor_world`:** C11 maps through `pose_q`, which includes the look-ahead `L`, and `L` is a function of this very aim; the loop (aim moves camera, camera moves the world point under a still cursor, which moves aim) would slew the beam towards a near cursor and keep it drifting after the mouse stops, with no cursor drawn to explain it. Measuring against `f_q` breaks the loop: `f_q` depends on the avatar's motion only, so with the avatar still a still cursor gives a constant `aim_q` while the look-ahead settles, and the beam still goes where the hidden cursor is *relative to the avatar*. The Adapter reads exactly two presentation values from the pipeline for this: `f_q` (published, pipeline D.14b) and the screen→picture mapping (`picture_centre`, `k_eff`); it reads no sim block for it beyond `body.state.pos_curr`. **Recorded trade-off** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R4)*: the aim is `cursor_aim_world − AIM_ORIGIN = (f_q − floor(pos_curr)) + cursor_off − (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y)`, so it is a function of the cursor, the follow lag `f_q − pos` and `k_eff`. With the avatar still the lag is zero and a still mouse gives a constant aim whatever the look-ahead does; **when a run starts or stops, `S = f_q − floor(pos_curr)` changes by at most 36 px at `v_run` (24 at walk): the lag part ≤ 32.4 px (the dt→0 bound; 30.9 px at 60 fps), the tick phase ≤ 3 px, floor 1 px (pipeline D.6, D.14b; D.7 variable `f_q`), and a still mouse turns the beam by the geometry of that shift** (about 31°, `atan(36/60)`, for a cursor 60 px from the avatar at full shift; about 10°, `atan(36/200)`, at 200 px), with no input from the player *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. This is accepted because the reference the hidden cursor is read against is the *picture* (the camera's follow pose), which is also what the player sees move; the review's alternative of anchoring on the avatar position would hold the beam rigid against the hand but put the hidden-cursor reference up to 104 px (32.4 px of lag plus the 72 px look-ahead) off the drawn avatar.
