*Cursor warp and source handover (one Adapter rule, presentation-local).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the 35 px origin offset does not scale with `k`, so a zoom step turned the beam under a still mouse, and the first mouse movement after stick use snapped the beam to a stale cursor position; the earlier acceptance criteria allowed both.)* The OS cursor is hidden and confined in `gameplay`, so the Adapter may reposition it without the player seeing a pointer move. **(i) Zoom edge:** on a `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` step (the pipeline's `RESCALING` frame) the Adapter warps the hidden cursor to `picture_centre + cursor_off_old × k_eff_new`, keeping `cursor_off` (base px) and therefore `aim_q` unchanged within ±1 unit; if the target position falls outside the window the warp clamps and the aim may differ (the confinement rectangle is the window, Edge Cases). **(ii) Handover to the mouse:** while the aim source is STICK or KEYS the mouse takes over only after `AIM_MOUSE_TAKEOVER_PX` (default 6 physical window px, **[PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike]**, range 2–16) of accumulated cursor travel, so a nudged desk does not hijack the lamp; at takeover the Adapter first warps the cursor to the point whose direction from `AIM_ORIGIN` is the current raw aim and whose radius is `max(last |r|, AIM_WARP_RADIUS_PX)` (default 48 base px, **[PLACEHOLDER]**, range 16–96), so the first mouse sample holds the aim it found instead of jumping to a stale position. **(iii) `aim_source` ∈ {AUTO, MOUSE, STICK, KEYS}:** `AUTO` (default) follows the last aim axis, with (ii) applied on a handover to the mouse; `MOUSE`, `STICK` or `KEYS` force one source and ignore the others (no handover, no warp on the forced source; the mouse stays warped only for (i)). A warp is Adapter-local presentation: it submits nothing, writes no block and reveals no sim state.

------
**PC-13. Devices, switching, rebinding.** **Glyphs follow the last button/key device** with `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS` = 250 ms; **aim source follows the last aim axis** independently; switching is silent, ≤ 1 frame, and **mixed input is permitted** (pad movement with mouse aim). The HR-11 focus bracket shows on key/pad navigation and hides on mouse motion. Godot merges devices per action, so an `interact` held on a pad survives touching the mouse. Switching aim source never jumps the beam (a stick release holds; a mouse move takes over). *Rebinding model* (MVP as data, Alpha as the screen): every action is bindable per device; conflicts are detected **per context** and never silently overwritten; no profile can lack a path to the chart table; presets include **one-handed** (`aim_release_mode = FOLLOW_ALWAYS`, run toggle on, channel toggle on, tap-to-confirm on). Every flow in the core loop is **gamepad-complete** (HR-14); text chat (VS-B) is the only keyboard-only item. **Keyboard bindings are by physical keycode** (`physical_keycode`), so WASD is the same four keys on AZERTY and QWERTZ layouts, and glyphs show the layout's own label (HUD's keycap grammar); **wheel events are coalesced** to at most one `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` edge per rendered frame (the net direction of that frame's wheel delta), so a notched or high-resolution wheel cannot walk the zoom ladder several steps in one frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

**PC-14. Position ownership — adopted (kernel Open Question 3 / pipeline Open Question 3 closed against Ship Body; technical-director ratification pending).** **Adopted: Ship Body owns ship-local integer position (`pos`, `sub`, `odometer`, `LocomotionStep`); the Controller Sim owns intent, gait, committed aim, facing, locomotion state, carry and channel references, chest point and hand point.** Contract: `controller.step` writes `octant`, `gait_effective`, `facing`, `loco_state`; `body.integrate` (divisor 1, `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)* runs `LocomotionStep` with `collide` bound to Layout's integer footprint rectangles (`SIMULATION` data) and commits `pos_prev / pos_curr`, `odometer`, `blocked`. *Why Body:* the composite welded ship is Body's (systems index high-risk row); an actor transfers between bodies (pod hop, detach) which Body tracks; and with no physics body the step is deterministic, so G3 needs no physics observations for crewmates. *Why not Controller:* it would put the Layout projection inside an input system. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Adopted by Ship Body & Interior Physics** (designed: its "Who owns what" section, BDY-7, BDY-9, BDY-10 take this split verbatim, and the foot box 16 × 8, the 1/256 fixed point and `trunc` rounding are Body's confirmed values); only the technical-director's ratification in the weld spike remains. Body's persisted `last_octant` (the octant its last step integrated) is a different field from this block's `last_octant` (the D.5 decel-ladder memory); both names are kept and the distinction is stated in PC-17.

**PC-15. Hook order and timing.** `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`) → `body.integrate` (divisor 1, `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`; owner Ship Body, BDY-8) → `controller.noise` (divisor 1, `after: [body.integrate]`; reads Body's derived `moved(actor_id)` and pushes the gait class, D.13) and `emitter.place` (divisor 1, `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`; beam emitter at the chest point for the exposure query) → Attention (divisor 6) integrates the pushed noise; a push landing after `attention.step` in a tick integrates on its next run (registry `push_stimulus`; Attention may add `controller.noise` to its own `after` list). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics, ship-section-and-layout-data-model, emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query, attention-system)* Input-to-effect: sampled before `Kernel.step()`, applied P2, integrated P3, drawn next render (≤ 17 ms + render latency).

**PC-16. Inputs owned here, consumed elsewhere.** `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` are two edge-triggered player inputs (pipeline C1) consumed by the pipeline's zoom ladder; `chart_table` calls `request_pause` (CR-15) through the menu in single-player and opens an overlay with the kernel `RUNNING` in co-op (CR-16); `inspect` enters the `inspect_card` context (the Adapter is the `INPUT_SURFACE` and owns the context; it publishes a presentation-local `{context, inspect_ref}` signal that In-World Instruments, a `PRESENTATION` surface, subscribe to — registry `inspect_card_context_signal`; never a command). The inspect card ships live at MVP (In-World Instruments IW-21). In `inspect_card`, `set_aim` stays live (the Adapter keeps sampling aim and sending `set_aim` as in `gameplay`), so the lamp can hold the gauge lit; the OS cursor stays hidden there (HUD HS-52; the mouse still steers the aim and picks nothing on the card, Instruments K-14) *(corrected 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view)* In `PAUSED` the Adapter submits no intents and resyncs on resume (PC-2).

**PC-17. Save, restore and co-op seams.** `controller.state` persists (`WORLD`). **The rest normalisation lives in `snapshot()`, not in `restore()`:** `snapshot()` writes the transient input fields at their rest values — `octant = NONE`, `run = false`, `channel_ref = none`, `channel_face = none` (so `face_octant` is never recomputed after a restore) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))*, `loco_state` as live except that `WALK`, `RUN`, `CARRY_WALK`, `CHANNELLING` and `STAGGERED` are written as `IDLE` (stagger timer cleared), so a persisted `octant == NONE` never sits beside a moving `loco_state` that Attention and Horror read as the class invariant, and the first `controller.step` after the restore recomputes the class member from the resynced intent by the step order of States and Transitions; `carry_ref`, `salvage_carry` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP; user ruling X3, delegated ruling R5)*, `facing`, `aim_angle` and `aim_live` as live *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* — and `restore()` validates into scratch, then replaces the block's contents in place (copying into the existing block object, never replacing the object; ADR-0006, root rule ADR-0003 § 2) and normalises nothing *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*, so `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is byte-identical in canonical bytes (kernel K:839, CR-8; Save/Load SL-15 item 10) and a loaded game still never resumes mid-move, mid-channel or mid-stagger. Integer vectors persist as two ints or a packed int array, never `Vector2i` (SL-2). This answers Save/Load OQ-9: `controller.state` is not in `REBASE_BLOCKS` (Save/Load's list, registry value `[interaction.state, assembly.state]`: `controller.state` and `body.state` are not listed, because the Controller normalises in `snapshot()` and BDY-31 makes Body's block restore-idempotent at block level); restore verification of this block is `EXACT`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* A restore restarts the run ramp (the resync re-sends `run`), so G4 fixtures walk across the snapshot tick. The kernel's `snap_baseline` on entry to RUNNING handles `previous`; Body only preserves `sub` (it resets on the first octant change, registry `move_octant_reset`) (pipeline C5; ADR-0008 § 6.1) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0008 sync)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format, ship-body-and-interior-physics)* VS-B: a guest's Adapter submits identically and the host's Controller Sim applies; `controller.state` and `body.state` replicate as `SHARED_SUMMARY`; remote crewmates' beams rotate from the **replicated committed aim, which may not be coarsened below the facing hysteresis** (1/64 turn) so facing agrees on every client; **no shared or assisted control** of any kind; the player's **own identity glyph** (beam shape + band count) sits on the suit panel; crewmate names are **press-to-reveal for ≈ 2 s and lit-only**; pings (if adopted) mark lit things only. Nothing in the Presenter branches on `HOST` / `MIRROR` (CR-10).

**PC-6. One focus model, interaction reach, lit-only actions, hold-to-confirm.** *Reach* is a sector from the foot origin: `REACH_PX` = 72 base px (1.5 tiles — the adjacent ring including diagonals at 68 px), half-angle `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` = 70° about the **facing**. Objects behind the player are never candidates. *Focus — the same model on every device:* among interactables that are in reach, in the arc and **lit** (Emitter State's exposure query above the technical-artist's threshold), the focused one minimises `score = d / REACH_PX + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × θ / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG`, with `θ` the angle between the object's direction from the foot origin and the **ground-projected aim** (mouse: the direction from the foot origin to `cursor_aim_world`, PC-5; stick and keys: the committed aim, a direction only) and `FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT` = 1.0 (0.5–2.0), `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` = 0.10 (D.9) — **aim-weighted proximity** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: measuring θ from the chest-height aim origin made a floor object the player points straight at read 30° off; the focus score is Adapter-side presentation, so the ground projection changes no sim value, and `in_reach` is untouched)*; the mouse has no separate pick-under-cursor path (the cursor moves the aim, and aim weights the score, so the model is one). Exactly one object is focused; the HUD draws its prompt (`E · Cut`) only when lit (art bible 7.0), at `world_to_hud(target)`; an off-screen object has no prompt (C9). **Self-target rule** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP, blocker PC-6 focus model)*: the candidate set has one fallback member, the actor's own suit (object class `ACTOR_SELF`). It is nominated if and only if (i) Suit's `tool_in_hand(player_id)` (the actor's own hand rail, SE-40, read like `carried_instance`) names a tool for which Interaction's declaration data has an `ACTOR_SELF` row (today `tool_welder`, the self-patch of IA-17; matched on the exact tool only, IA-5 tier (1), no `NEEDS_TOOL` fallback), (ii) `carry_ref == none` and `loco_state ∉ {DOWNED, DEAD, IN_POD}`, and (iii) the world candidate set (in reach, in arc, lit) is empty. It is the focus only while (iii) holds: any world candidate displaces it on the frame that candidate appears, and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` never holds the self-target against a world candidate. Its score is `SELF_FOCUS_SCORE = 2 + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × 180 / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG + FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (D.9), load-computed and not a knob (4.67 at defaults), so it is above every world score. The Adapter submits `begin_pa

**PC-7. Channels (cut / weld / patch).** `interact` on an object whose declared mode is `CHANNEL` → the Adapter submits `begin_<verb> {target}` (`coalesce = NONE`; owner Interaction, Assembly behind it for weld/cut). The owner's `validate` requires: lit and in reach, except an `ACTOR_SELF` channel (no lit or reach test, PC-6) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; conformance)*, **`controller.state.intent_octant == NONE`**, not carrying, not staggered/downed. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `intent_octant` and `intent_run` are written by the `set_move_intent` `apply` handler in P2; `octant` is the value `controller.step` publishes in P3 and the channel owners' hooks read. Validation that read `octant` saw last tick's value, so releasing W and pressing E in one frame was rejected, and pressing W and E together was accepted and then aborted silently. With the split the first applies and the second is rejected at once with reason `MOVING` (immediate class, "no" cue; proposed to Interaction, today folded into `BUSY` — Open Question 25). Both rely on the Adapter submitting intents before commands in a frame (PC-2).)* **Progress is sim state in `interaction.state`** (with `owner_system` ASSEMBLY for weld and section cut), accrued per tick by Interaction's hook; the owner's `apply` records `channel_ref`, `channel_face` and `channel_body` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; INTERNAL fix)* through the Controller's `set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant)` mutator (PC-1 b) and the Controller holds facing at `channel_face` (PC-4 rule 2); `loco_state` becomes `CHANNELLING` in that tick's `controller.step` by the precedence function of States and Transitions *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, interaction-system)* **Hold is the default; a toggle option exists; both are Adapter policy over the same two commands.** *Interrupts:* (i) **release** (hold mode) or a second press / `cancel` (toggle mode) → `cancel_channel`; (ii) **movement** — `controller.step` itself clears `channel_ref` and `channel_face` in the tick an applied intent has `octant ≠ NONE` (step 3 of the `controller.step` order, so the move wins on that same tick and the first movement step is not lost), and the owner's hook, declared `after: controller.step`, reads `controller.state.octant` and aborts (sim-side, so identical in `MIRROR`; the 8-way dead-zone already filters stick drift) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (iii) **stagger / downed** — the Controller Sim 

**PC-8. Carrying.** `pickup` (Interaction) sets `controller.state.carry_ref` through `set_carry_ref`; `carry_drop` → `drop` clears it through `clear_carry_ref` (PC-1 b; Assembly also calls `clear_carry_ref` on an install). While carrying: gait forced to `v_carry` (**no run while carrying** — no carry-run cycle exists and a sprinting module is the wrong image); every `interact` mode except `drop` and the declared carry-admitted rows — `install_module` (`interact` on a HARDPOINT subject whose `compatible_defs(h)` lists the carried instance's def) and `pod_hop` on the CONSOLE, and V4 `set_opening` on a door face (the row Interaction flags `admitted_while_carrying`, IA-28: a lit, in-reach, bare-hand TAP needs no free hands; `carry_ref`, the carry gait and the beam are unchanged; the door's attempt window is Interaction's, IA-24) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* — is rejected `BUSY` (hands full); `begin_patch`, `begin_cut`, `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut` stay `BUSY`, and a V6 vent-hatch `set_opening` is not carry-admitted; the beam **stays available** (user decision 2026-10-26 — chest lamp; the carry frames keep the chest point and the forward beam arc clear; overhead at MVP (art-director, AD-BS-1)). *Playtest lever only (the 2026-10-26 user decision — beam available — stands):* beam **off** while carrying — extraction in the dark — is a strong Pillar 3 lever that changes the sortie's difficulty curve more than any other single rule here. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, boarding-and-salvage, interaction-system)* Stagger does **not** drop the module; downed does. **Salvage carry** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP; user ruling X3, delegated ruling R5)*: when `set_carry_ref(actor, item_id)` takes `carry_ref` from none to an item it also sets `controller.state.salvage_carry := body_of_actor(actor) != HOME_BODY` (a Ship Body read at the pickup tick; `HOME_BODY` is the player's home ship body, a derelict welded to it being part of it); `salvage_carry` is kept across `pod_hop` and a weld (the item stays a salvage carry) and clears to false whenever `carry_ref` clears (drop, install, throw, the downed drop, `clear_carry_ref`, a restore of a none `carry_ref`). `carry_ref` and `salvage_carry` are published as `SIM` reads for Attention's item-keyed rearm (AT-10) and drive the BURDEN push (PC-10, D.13).

**PC-9. Honest body states: stagger, downed, dead — driven by the sim, never by a stat.** The Controller Sim reads one value from Suit & Equipment's view (`after: suit.vitals`, divisor 6 — a read up to 5 ticks old is tolerated): **`locomotion_cap` ∈ {FULL, WALK_ONLY, NONE}**, which Suit derives from O₂, temperature and suit integrity (its thresholds; its internal vitals ladder is not read here) — block `suit.state`, field `locomotion_cap`: FULL while the worst rung ≤ 1, WALK_ONLY at rung 2 (CRITICAL), NONE at rung 3 (FAILED) (registry `vitals_ladder_step`; SE-16 to SE-19, SE-24). Rules: `FULL` — no effect (rime and visor fog are Suit-driven overlays the Presenter shows; information, not penalties). **Edge detection is against a stored value, `controller.state.cap_seen`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the edge needs a previous cap and none was stored, so behaviour after a restore while the cap was `WALK_ONLY` was undefined: staggered on every load or never)*: each tick `controller.step` reads the cap, compares it with `cap_seen`, acts on the edge, then writes `cap_seen := cap` — **in every state, including `DOWNED`, `DEAD` and `IN_POD`**, so no edge is ever remembered across a state that ignored it. `cap_seen` is persisted (PC-17); `post_restore` re-reads the cap and sets `cap_seen := cap`, so **a restore never produces an edge** (restoring with the cap at `WALK_ONLY` does not stagger). A cap edge while already `STAGGERED` neither restarts nor extends the timer (`stagger_end_tick` keeps its value; it still updates `cap_seen`). Worked sequence `FULL → NONE → WALK_ONLY → FULL → WALK_ONLY`: `NONE` is `DOWNED` with no stagger; `NONE → WALK_ONLY` is a rising edge (`DOWNED →` the locomotion-class member, no stagger); `WALK_ONLY → FULL` is nothing; the final `FULL → WALK_ONLY` is the only falling edge: exactly **one** stagger. **Falling edge `FULL → WALK_ONLY`** → one **stagger** (`STAGGER_TICKS` = 30; input ignored; channel cleared; no displacement — a stagger is animation plus input lock, never an impulse), then **walk only** while the cap holds (the `run` action does nothing; the HUD breath/warmth readings and the visor fog are the readable reason — no banner). **`NONE`** → **downed** (down 6, input ignored, carry dropped); in MVP solo, downed → **dead** after `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` = 1800 unless the cap rises, **or at once when the player gives up**: while `DOWNED` in solo the `give_up` action (hold-to-confirm, PC-2) submits `give_up {actor}`, which lowers `death_tick` to the apply tick, so the same D.14 c

**PC-10. The two rhythms in the controller.** Nothing in this system changes between boarding, the Tell and breach: no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise, no "panic" input changes. **The breach is frantic because of what moves, not because the body changes** (art bible 2.8). Running is allowed everywhere and is **noisy**: the hook `controller.noise` (divisor 1, `after: [body.integrate]`, D.13) calls Attention's `push_stimulus(NOISE, actor, class)` once on each tick the actor moved, with `class` = WALK, RUN or CARRY from `loco_state`; the class magnitudes are this GDD's gait table `NOISE_WALK` = 1, `NOISE_RUN` = 4, `NOISE_CARRY` = 1 (registry: `NOISE_PER_TICK`; Attention units, 1 AU = one walking tick). Running is 1.5× faster and 4× louder per tick, ≈ 2.7× louder per tile: running never dominates walking for stealth and is a real trade in a retreat. The player's **own running footsteps are audible and distinct from walking** — the only "meter" for noise (audio-director; captions name "your running" for the accessibility-specialist). Tool noise is pushed by Interaction (classes TOOL / LOUD); Suit pushes none at MVP; beam exposure is Emitter State's. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from attention-system, ship-body-and-interior-physics)* **The BURDEN push** (user ruling X3; delegated ruling R5; Attention AT-3 row `BURDEN`, F-26; registry `carry_burden_intake`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP; user ruling X3, delegated ruling R5)*: the same hook `controller.noise` (divisor 1, after `body.integrate`) also calls `push_stimulus(NOISE, actor, BURDEN)` once on **every** tick, moving, standing or channelling, on which `carry_ref != none` and `salvage_carry` is true and the holder's current body `body_of_actor(actor)` (read after `body.integrate`, so it is this tick's body of the holder's `actor_section`, Ship Body CP-3) is a non-home locus body and `loco_state` ∉ {`IN_POD`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD`}; it pushes nothing otherwise (a stowed item is not carried; carrying at home; the player's own kit; the pod leg). The magnitude is `U_BURDEN` (registry; Attention's unit, 7 AU [PLACEHOLDER], cited here, not defined); the push is keyed on the carry state and never on `mass_g` (IDB-21), and it is **in addition to** the CARRY gait push on a tick that moved. The moved-only gate of `noise_T` (D.13) applies to the gait classes only; the BURDEN push fires whether or not the actor moved. `controller.noise` carries it because `controller.step` runs before `body.integrate` and cannot see this tick's body (Ship Body CP-3

**PC-11. Animation is distance-driven; the human channel; the controller never renders.** Body accumulates an integer **`odometer`** from pixels actually moved post-collision (an actor walking into a wall does not animate); the Presenter's frame is `floor(odometer / stride) mod 8` with `STRIDE_WALK` = 10, `STRIDE_RUN` = 15, `STRIDE_CARRY` = 5 base px — 12 fps at every gait. Work, stagger and down are time-stepped at 12 fps and idle breathing at 24 ticks per frame, all from committed tick counts. The crewmate sprite and its beam are inviolable anchors (Pillar 1; art bible 5.0). This system draws nothing: the Presenter reads committed state; the Perception Filter may substitute the whole body for a horror rig (5.0) but never edits pixels, moves the chest or hand point or touches the beam. Remote crewmates are drawn by the same Presenter from `MIRROR` state (PC-17). Haptics are driven by P1 physical events only (HR-6).

**PC-12. What the player cannot do.** No jump, dodge-roll, vault, lean/peek (C9), melee or attack input (anti-pillar: not a combat game — the friendly-harm act is an Interaction verb on a crewmate target under Sanity's gate, reached through `interact`, never a dedicated button), no auto-aim, magnetism or aim assist of any kind, no acrobatics, no QTEs, no sprint-by-deflection. **No crouch (decided).** *Rationale:* restraint is *light and noise* (Pillar 3), not posture; a quieter crouch is a free dodge every player would hold permanently (Sirlin: a dominant non-decision); the sheet budget has no crouch set; a curled crewmate drifts toward the horror grammar 5.2 forbids. Walking with the beam off *is* the quiet stance.

**D.10 Hold-to-confirm bar and tap-to-confirm**

The `confirm_bar` formula (Adapter-local, render time) is defined as:

`Δt_eff = 0 if kernel PAUSED else min(Δt, CONFIRM_DT_MAX_S);  b ← clamp(b + Δt_eff / CONFIRM_HOLD_S, 0, 1) while held;  b ← max(b − CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE × Δt_eff / CONFIRM_HOLD_S, 0) while released;  on b ≥ 1: submit the declared command once, b ← 0, require release before re-arm` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the bar added uncapped wall time per frame, so one 1 s hitch confirmed a destructive cut; re-review: the bar **freezes** under `PAUSED` (`Δt_eff = 0`; it neither fills nor drains), so a destructive hold can never complete during a pause and be rejected `PAUSED`, and on resume the hold continues only if the button is still down — the PC-2 resync submits the cancel otherwise)*

Derived (target latch): while `b > 0` the bar belongs to the focus `o_latched` captured when `b` left zero; a focus change does not move or complete it (it drains at 2× on `o_latched`, then the new focus starts from 0); completion submits for `o_latched` only
Derived (`give_up` surface) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the bar for `give_up` is drawn by HUD's DOWNED-only confirm plate (UI Requirements 1) from `confirm_view(seat)`; the plate exists for the whole time `loco_state == DOWNED` (published as `confirm_view.give_up_live`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and the bar arms only from a press edge observed while DOWNED (Edge Cases); the bar starts accumulating on the frame **after** the press edge, so with one rendered frame per tick the 0.8 s default fills 48 frames after the edge
Derived (per-verb hold; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D80 and D81; X10 is ruled) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: in the formula above read `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` as the verb's effective hold `H_v = min(m_v × confirm_hold_s, cap_v)` (`cap_v` ≤ `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S`, below), where `confirm_hold_s` is the player's adjustable base hold (default `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` = 0.8 s), `m_v` is the multiplier the verb's owner declares (1 for every verb except the Chart Table's slot Delete, which declares 2, so Delete holds **1.6 s** at the default), and `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S` = 1.9 s is the ceiling that keeps invariant 7 true for every verb (derivation below). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-19 / C-10)* The formula is `H_v = min(m_v × confirm_hold_s, cap_v)`, where `m_v` and `cap_v` are declared by the verb's owner; `cap_v` defaults to `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S` and may never exceed it. The Chart Table declares `cap_v = CT_HOLD_CAP_S = HOLD_EFF_MAX_S − DELETE_MARGIN_MIN_S = 1.9 − 0.4 = 1.5 s` for its quit-without-saving (UI-3) and Retire (UI-5) holds (`m_v` 1), and `cap_v = HOLD_EFF_MAX_S` for slot Delete (`m_v` 2), so Delete exceeds every other Chart Table hold by at least 0.4 s at every base hold; the Settings range of `confirm_hold_s` (0.6–1.9 s, user ruling X10) is not reduced. A player who cannot hold at all uses `confirm_mode = TAP` (two taps within `CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW`), which is selectable in Settings at MVP and not only in the one-handed preset
Derived (tap mode): tap 1 on focus `o` → `armed(o)` until `t_arm + CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW`, where `t_arm` and the window advance only while the kernel is not `PAUSED` (the timer is frozen under pause); tap 2 within the window on the same `o` → submit; focus change, context change or expiry → disarmed

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| Δt | float | render frame s | calculated (the frame's `render_delta`, clamped by the presentation driver, ADR-0009) | Frame delta — real time, never a `Time.*` read (ADR-0010 SIM-02); the sim never sees the bar *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0010 sync)* |
| CONFIRM_HOLD_S (registry: `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`) | float | 0.6–1.9 (**0.8**) render s *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: was 0.6–1.2)* | data file; the player-adjustable Settings value `confirm_hold_s` starts here | Hold needed to confirm a destructive verb (base hold, before the verb multiplier) |
| m_v *(user rulings)* | int | {1, 2} (**1**; slot Delete **2**) | declared by the verb's owner (Interaction; Chart Table for Delete) | Per-verb multiple of the base hold; the owner also declares `cap_v` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-19 / C-10)* |
| cap_v | float | ≤ `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S` (1.9 default); Chart Table non-Delete holds 1.5 | declared by the verb's owner | Per-verb ceiling on the effective hold *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-19 / C-10)* |
| HOLD_EFF_MAX_S *(user rulings)* | float | 1.9 render s (derived) | calculated: `floor(10 × (max_age_ticks − 1) / TICK_RATE) / 10` = `floor(10 × 119 / 60) / 10` = 1.9 | Cap on any effective hold `H_v`; keeps `H_v × TICK_RATE = 114 < 120 = max_age_ticks(actions)` (invariant 7) at the largest base hold and the largest multiplier |

## Decision

### 1. The tick source is `_process`, in one host node

A single `KernelHost` node (`src/game/kernel_host.gd`; `extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`) owns a `TickDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls it from its own `_process(delta)`. The host does one thing with the engine's `delta`: it converts it once, `delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0))`, and passes the integer to the driver. That conversion and the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads **that reach the simulation** (kernel H9). Which files may read clocks at all is the SIM-02 allow-list owned by ADR-0010 (`kernel_host.gd`, `monotonic_clock.gd`, `system_wall_clock.gd` and the diagnostics timer; TD-11, TD-14); the injected `MonotonicClock` and the Save/Load-only `WallClock` port are not kernel inputs. Presentation has exactly one `_process`: the single presentation host's (the Pipeline root, `PipelineRoot`; ADR-0008 § 6.1, ADR-0009), at `ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, which advances `present_time` and drives the presenter stages (camera smoothing and cosmetic accumulators live in those stages; Pipeline PR-9; Chart Table CT-43). Presenters define no `_process`. Presentation may read the committed tick `T` where the sim also computes the value (for example `beacon_aim(T)`, LO-27); none of that feeds back into the simulation. The driver is exactly the one specified in kernel CR-1a and D.5: an integer accumulator in units of microseconds × `TICK_RATE` (`TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 per tick), a boundary service before any tick, `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)`, a re-read of the kernel state after every `step()`, lag forgiveness (`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0), result flush, and the paused service. This ADR does not restate those rules; the GDD is their authority. It records the *placement* and *order* decisions below.

**`TickDriver.frame()` is a two-statement wrapper** (TD-04; ADR-0004 § 5): `_frame_body(delta_us)` runs the CR-1a steps and may return early (a pause, a restore request, a fault, a zero-tick frame), and then `_kernel.deliver_frame_end()` runs unconditionally, with no other statement after the body. Because GDScript has no `finally`, the early returns live in `_frame_body` and the delivery lives outside it, so no exit path can skip frame-end delivery. The per-frame result is written into a reused `TickFrameResult` that callers read from `driver.last_result` (so `frame()` returns nothing and has no statement after the delivery). Test KRN-FRAME-END (Validation Criteria) proves it.

**The physics callback is not the clock and is not used by any simulation or presentation code in the MVP.** No script in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/` defines `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces`; `physics_interpolation` stays off. The kernel does not read `physics_jitter_fix`, `physics_ticks_per_second` or `max_physics_steps_per_frame`, and nothing is coupled to them, **but they can shape the `delta` the host receives** (the engine's main-loop timer sync produces both, UNVERIFIED), so the spike logs delta jitter at `physics_jitter_fix` 0.5 and at 0. Determinism does not depend on it, because replays inject `delta_us`. A boot check records `physics_ticks_per_second != TICK_RATE` in the diagnostics header as information, not as a failure. A later Vertical Slice physics projection (ADR-0033) runs in `_physics_process` as a read-only PROJECTOR and never steps the kernel.

### 2. Frame order is fixed by named priority constants

Godot runs `_process` in ascending `process_priority`, ties broken by tree order. Tree order is not a contract we want to depend on, so the order is fixed by four constants in one file, `src/kernel/process_priority.gd`:

```gdscript
class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted

## Lower values run first inside one rendered frame.
const INPUT_ADAPTER: int = -100   # INPUT_SURFACE objects only; samples input, calls submit()
const TICK_DRIVER: int = -50      # KernelHost: boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, result flush, frame-end delivery
const HOST_SERVICE: int = -40     # SaveHost (ADR-0006) only: per-frame poll after the driver; observes the last committed tick boundary
const PRESENTATION: int = 0       # engine default; the single presentation host (PipelineRoot), so a node that forgets to set it still runs after the driver
```

The order is therefore **input adapter → tick driver → host service (SaveHost) → presentation**, matching the kernel GDD's priority table (its ordinals 0, 1 and 2 are order only; the values above are the implementation; `HOST_SERVICE` is the one addition and sits between the driver and presentation). `HOST_SERVICE` is named and valued once, here, and is used by `SaveHost` only (ADR-0006, TD-04, TD-10); there is no `PRESENTATION_LATE` constant (TD-03: the single presentation host removes the need). Choosing `PRESENTATION` as the engine default is deliberate: an unset node lands after the driver, which is the safe failure.

Rules, each of which becomes a lint (ADR-0010):
- A node whose `process_priority` is below `TICK_DRIVER` must be a registered INPUT_SURFACE object. Nothing else may run before the driver. Scene files (`.tscn`) must not set `process_priority` at all (the Inspector stores a literal); code sets it from `ProcessPriority`. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime, so the authoritative check is a **boot-time tree walk** (ADR-0010 KRN-05): every node whose priority is below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE object, only `KernelHost` uses `TICK_DRIVER`'s value, only `SaveHost` uses `HOST_SERVICE`'s value (the known-node set below `PRESENTATION` is the registered INPUT_SURFACE objects, `KernelHost` and `SaveHost`), and every INPUT_SURFACE, `KernelHost`, `SaveHost` and presentation node resolves to the main-thread `process_thread_group`, because a sub-thread group leaves the main-thread ordering and breaks the main-thread rule. `process_thread_group` defaults to `INHERIT`, so the walk resolves each node's **effective** group by following `INHERIT` up through its ancestors to the first explicit value (the root counts as `MAIN_THREAD`); reading the node's own property alone would pass an `INHERIT` node under a `SUB_THREAD` parent. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review.)* Exactly which rules the lint tool can enforce statically and which move to boot walks is ADR-0010's call (OQ-16).
- No node other than `KernelHost` may use `TICK_DRIVER`'s value, and no node other than `SaveHost` may use `HOST_SERVICE`'s value.
- A presentation node's `process_priority` is `PRESENTATION` or greater and is never set to a literal; it references the constant. The presentation host is the one `_process` in presentation (ADR-0008 § 6.1, ADR-0009); layer 3 and 4 UI Controls and registered INPUT_SURFACE objects keep the exemptions ADR-0009 lists.
- Code in `src/sim/` and `src/presentation/` does not `await get_tree().process_frame` (that signal fires outside the per-node ordering, UNVERIFIED); waiting is expressed in ticks or in `present_time`.

### 3. The Input Adapter samples and submits in its own `_process`

The Adapter (an INPUT_SURFACE, Player Controller GDD PC-1(a)) reads device state and calls `submit()` from its `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`. It may latch raw events in `_input`/`_unhandled_input`, which the engine delivers before the frame's `_process` calls, but it submits only from `_process`. Its commands are therefore queued before the driver's boundary service and tick loop run, so an intent sampled in frame N sits in tick T's P1 batch, is applied in P2 and is integrated in P3 of the same tick: one tick of latency, never two. The Adapter never samples in `_physics_process`. Devices are identified by event type, not by `device == 0` (4.7 changed mouse and keyboard device IDs; ADR-0019).

In a frame that runs several ticks (catch-up), the Adapter has submitted once, so only the first tick of that frame sees new commands. Continuing movement survives because intent state lives in `controller.state` and commands are edge- or change-based, not per-tick.

### 4. `tick_alpha` is the only value presentation reads *from the driver*

At the end of each driver frame the driver publishes `tick_alpha = clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0.0, 1.0)` (identical to kernel D.3's `t_since_last_commit / tick_duration`; the casts are required, because `acc` and `TICK_UNITS` are both `int` and an unmarked `/` is integer division in GDScript, which would give 0 on every normal frame and fail the `integer_division` warning policy). It is a presentation-only float: it is not a state block, is never hashed or saved, and the simulation never reads it (kernel H9). Presentation reads it once per frame, through `PresentationClock`, in the single presentation host's `_process` (the driver stages fill `PresentFrame`; ADR-0009) and interpolates previous-to-current committed state with `pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) * tick_alpha)` (Pipeline Section D, interpolation formula; restore case in its Edge Cases). Because forgiveness at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0 drops whole lag ticks at the end of every frame but keeps the sub-tick remainder, `acc < TICK_UNITS` after the driver runs in `RUNNING`, so `tick_alpha` is continuous and in [0, 1). **Two rules from kernel D.3 are binding and are restated here because they are easy to lose:** (1) **while the kernel is not `RUNNING` the driver holds `tick_alpha` at 1.0**, so a paused, loading or saving game draws the latest committed pose and never a frozen partway-back pose; (2) **on every transition into `RUNNING` the kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every `interpolated` block** (ADR-0003), so `previous == current` on resume and the first running frame, including a 0-tick frame, cannot interpolate across a discontinuity. **This kernel call is the only restore-continuity mechanism** (TD-22): ADR-0008 has no `previous := current` rule of its own in `post_restore`, and the camera's `DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE` CUT fires on a change of `PresentationClock.load_seq` (§ 5).

Presentation also keeps a render-rate cosmetic clock, `present_time`, owned by the Pipeline root (Pipeline PR-9, ADR-0008). The rule recorded here: **cosmetic phase (flicker, gutter, fades) uses `present_time`; anything the simulation also computes (beacon aim, poses, wane) uses the kernel tick; the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase** (Lighting LO-4).

### 5. The kernel reaches modules by injection

There is no `Kernel` autoload and no static singleton for kernel or game state. The main scene's root script (the **composition root**, `src/game/game.gd`) constructs the kernel, the `TickDriver` and the `KernelHost`, then gives every module and subscriber **the narrowest facet it needs through `setup()`**, never the whole `Kernel`: a simulation module receives the registration and mutator-scope services ADR-0003 defines; a presentation subscriber receives `subscribe(...)`, the read views and a read-only **`PresentationClock`** (`tick_alpha`, `T`, `running`, `state`, `load_seq`, backed by the driver and kernel); the composition root issues the **`NotifyFacet`**, binding the subscriber class at issue (ADR-0004 § 2), so a holder cannot subscribe as a class it was not issued; and the right to submit or to call the control plane comes only from the named handles ADR-0002 defines, which the root issues to a few objects. The kernel-state need of presentation (ADR-0008) is met by `PresentationClock.state`, not by a separate `KernelStateView` type. **Restore marker:** `PresentationClock.load_seq` is incremented by the kernel on every `LOADING → RUNNING` transition (a restore and a new game), immediately before `deliver_all` (ADR-0004), and never on `PAUSED → RUNNING` or `SAVING → RUNNING`; presentation compares it with the last value it saw to detect a discontinuity (ADR-0008 camera CUT, ADR-0009 `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)`). `ChangeBatch` carries no load flag by design (ADR-0004 § 6). Handing the whole kernel to presentation would give it `submit()`, which kernel CR-10 limits to INPUT_SURFACE. Headless tests construct their own kernel, driver and facets and need no scene. In the code examples in `docs/architecture/architecture.md`, `Kernel.` reads as "the injected facet". There are no recorded exceptions.

### 6. Pause, load and the tree

The kernel's `PAUSED` state is the only pause the simulation knows (kernel CR-16). `KernelHost` is `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, so the driver keeps running its boundary service whether or not anything pauses the scene tree, and no simulation code reads `SceneTree.paused`. Whether the UI layers use `SceneTree.paused` or per-layer `process_mode` is **not decided here**: the Chart Table GDD routes it to its own ADR candidate (a) and the Debug Overlay GDD (E-DO-48, AC-DO-174) assumes `SceneTree.paused` can be true; ADR-0030 decides it, and it must keep `KernelHost`, `SaveHost` (ADR-0006) and the Input Adapter `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. Window focus loss, an OS-level stall, a debugger break or a long load simply produces one large `delta`: the cap (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4) and forgiveness absorb it, and the accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`, so loads, saves and pauses never cause catch-up bursts afterwards (kernel CR-1a).

### Key Interfaces

```gdscript
class_name TickDriver extends RefCounted
## Turns an injected wall-time delta into whole kernel ticks. No scene tree, no engine clock.
func _init(kernel: Kernel, params: TickParams) -> void
func frame(delta_us: int) -> void              # exactly two statements: _frame_body(delta_us) then _kernel.deliver_frame_end(); nothing after the body
func _frame_body(delta_us: int) -> void        # boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, flush, paused service; may return early (pause, restore request, fault)
var last_result: TickFrameResult:              # reused object filled by _frame_body: ticks_run, dropped, tick_alpha
	get: return _result
var tick_alpha: float:                         # presentation-only; read once per frame
	get: return _tick_alpha

class_name KernelHost extends Node             # src/game/kernel_host.gd
func setup(driver: TickDriver) -> void         # called by the composition root; sets process_mode and process_priority = ProcessPriority.TICK_DRIVER
func _process(delta: float) -> void            # returns at once if setup() has not run (null driver); else delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0)); driver.frame(delta_us)

class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted  # INPUT_ADAPTER -100, TICK_DRIVER -50, HOST_SERVICE -40, PRESENTATION 0 (Decision § 2)

# Issued by the composition root; the subscriber class is bound at issue (ADR-0004 § 2)
class_name NotifyFacet extends RefCounted      # subscribe only; signature and class binding owned by ADR-0004

# Every module and subscriber:
func setup(facet: ModuleFacet) -> void         # the narrowest facet for the module's class (ADR-0003 / ADR-0009); stored; never looked up through a global

class_name PresentationClock extends RefCounted  # read-only, backed by the TickDriver and the kernel
var tick_alpha: float:
	get: return _driver.tick_alpha                 # 1.0 while the kernel is not RUNNING
var T: int:
	get: return _kernel_clock_t()                  # last committed tick
var running: bool:
	get: return _kernel_running()
var state: int:
	get: return _kernel_state()                    # the kernel state enum value (as defined by the kernel GDD); replaces any KernelStateView type
var load_seq: int:
	get: return _kernel_load_seq()                 # +1 by the kernel on every LOADING -> RUNNING (restore and new game), immediately before deliver_all; never on PAUSED/SAVING -> RUNNING
```

### Implementation Guidelines
- **Must** drive `Kernel.step()` only from `TickDriver.frame()`, and call `TickDriver.frame()` only from `KernelHost._process`. Tests may call either directly.
- **Must** keep `TickDriver.frame()` to two statements, `_frame_body(...)` then `_kernel.deliver_frame_end()`; **must never** add a statement after the delivery or an early `return` in `frame()` itself.
- **Must** increment `load_seq` only on `LOADING → RUNNING`, once per transition, immediately before `deliver_all`; **must never** increment it on `PAUSED → RUNNING` or `SAVING → RUNNING`, and **must never** add a load flag to `ChangeBatch`.
- **Must** use `ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE` only in `SaveHost`.
- **Must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/`.
- **Must** use the `ProcessPriority` constants; **must never** write a literal `process_priority` value.
- **Must** submit input only from the Input Adapter's `_process`; **must never** call `submit()` from `_input`, `_physics_process` or a signal handler.
- **Must** pass each module its facet with `setup()`; **must never** add an autoload, a static variable or a group lookup that exposes the kernel, a block or a read view, and **must never** give a presentation node the whole `Kernel`.
- **Must** read `tick_alpha` through `PresentationClock` in presentation only, never in a simulation callable, and **must never** use the tick counter for cosmetic animation phase.
- **Must** keep `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` in release builds; a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise. A boot assertion also requires `application/run/low_processor_mode` to be false (in low-processor mode the engine idles between events, the simulation would stall and the next `delta` would spike), and the diagnostics header records `Engine.max_fps`, the vsync mode and `physics_ticks_per_second`.
- **Must** pin the tick contract with a unit test: `TICK_RATE` = 60 and `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4 (kernel CR-1a), and `_physics_process` absent from `src/kernel`, `src/sim` and `src/presentation` (the existing lint). Both are set-once code constants of the kernel GDD, not data, so a runtime boot check could never fail; the test fails CI on any change instead, and no fault code is needed. Every duration in the Modular Ship Assembly GDD (AS-42) is counted in ticks at that rate, so a different rate or catch-up bound would silently change it (TR-assembly-042).
- **Must** keep the `delta_us` conversion in `KernelHost` and nowhere else. The forbidden clock and RNG token list and its allow-list are owned by ADR-0010 `SIM-02` (allow-list: `kernel_host.gd`, `monotonic_clock.gd`, `system_wall_clock.gd` and the diagnostics timer; TD-11, TD-14); this ADR keeps no list of its own. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review; list replaced by the pointer under TD-04/TD-14.)*
- **Should** test the driver with injected `delta_us` sequences (16,000 / 16,667 / 17,334 µs patterns, 100 ms hitches, zero-length frames) and the frame order with a recording scene (KRN-LAT-01, KRN-LAT-02).

## Decision

### 1. Capability handles are the only way in

There is no global `submit`. The composition root (ADR-0001) holds the kernel in `BOOTING` and issues two kinds of handle, each by name, each once:

```gdscript
# Issued only in BOOTING by the composition root. Names appear in diagnostics.
var surface: SurfaceHandle = kernel.issue_surface_handle(&"input_adapter")   # may submit PLAYER commands
var control: ControlHandle = kernel.issue_control_handle(&"save_load")       # host-local control plane
```

- A **`SurfaceHandle`** carries `submit(type, payload, actor, correlation)` and a result handler. It is stamped at issue time with the origin `PLAYER` and the `issuer_peer` it represents (`HOST_PEER_ID` = `MultiplayerPeer.TARGET_PEER_SERVER`, value 1, for every local surface; the constant is defined from the engine name, not the literal). At MVP exactly one surface is issued, to the Input Adapter (the Chart Table submits zero commands at MVP; a second surface is issued only when a system genuinely needs one, and is named at issue). **Holding a `SurfaceHandle` and subscribing as `INPUT_SURFACE` are separate rights:** subscribing in that class (CR-10) means receiving every tick's batch; it does not give submit rights, and the Interaction prompt object subscribes as INPUT_SURFACE without a handle. "Presentation never submits" is therefore enforced by a **state guard plus a lint**, not by construction: `Kernel` exposes no public submit or control method (both live only on handles); `issue_*_handle` refuses outside `BOOTING`; presentation subscribes only after registration freezes; and a CI check forbids calls to `_`-prefixed kernel members from outside `src/kernel/`, because GDScript has no private members.
- A **`ControlHandle`** carries the host-local control plane (§ 6). It is issued to Save/Load (`save_load`), the Chart Table's `PauseGate` (`pause_gate`) and the composition root (`game`); nobody else gets one.
- **SYSTEM-origin submission is not a handle.** `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key)` and `has_pending(type, dedupe_key)` are methods of the `HookContext` and `ApplyContext` objects the kernel passes into step hooks and `apply` (ADR-0003 defines the contexts). A SYSTEM command can therefore only be created inside a tick phase, by a registered owner, and never from a signal handler or `_process`. The test ingress (§ 8) is the one other caller.
- Handles are issued only while the kernel is `BOOTING` (like every registration, CR-6) and are not serialisable. Handle names are unique; a duplicate fails boot.
- Handles are plain `RefCounted` objects passed by `setup()` (ADR-0001). Holding a reference is the capability.
- **A forged handle fails closed.** GDScript cannot stop `SurfaceHandle.new()`, so a handle carries an integer slot id and a token that the kernel wrote into its issued-handle table at issue time. `submit` forwards both to `_admit`, which checks the pair against the table; an unregistered or mismatched handle logs `push_error`, counts `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED` in diagnostics and returns without admitting anything. Nothing relies on the lint alone.
- **No reference cycle.** The kernel stores handles only as slot ids and tokens (never as object references), and a handle holds the kernel, so the pair is a one-way reference. `Kernel.shutdown()` clears the table.
- **Result handlers are method Callables, cleared on teardown.** The handler passed to `set_result_handler` must be a method Callable on a long-lived object (a lambda that captures `self` creates a handle → Callable → owner → handle cycle that GDScript's reference counting leaks). The owner calls `clear_result_handler()` from its `_exit_tree`. At flush the kernel checks `handler.is_valid()` before every call and drops an invalid handler with a diagnostics count `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`.

### 2. One ingress function stamps every command

All paths (surface handle, `submit_system`, the future remote ingress, the test ingress) call one kernel-private function:

```gdscript
func _admit(origin: int, issuer_peer: int, type: StringName, payload: Dictionary,
		actor: int, correlation: int, supplied_seq: int) -> void   # supplied_seq only from the test or remote ingress
```

It performs, in order: stamp `submission_id` (a kernel-unique counter, so even a rejected submit has one) → stamp `seq` from the one kernel-held counter for `(issuer_peer, origin)` unless the test or remote ingress supplied one → resolve the type (`UNKNOWN_TYPE`) → check kernel state (`NOT_ACCEPTING`; `PAUSED` unless the type is `allowed_when_paused`) → origin allowed for the type (`ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`) → duplicate `seq` (`DUPLICATE_SEQ`, test and remote only) → rate limit (`RATE_LIMITED`, remote only) → payload walk, size and schema (`MALFORMED`) → coalescing (§ 5) → queue capacity (`QUEUE_FULL`) → enqueue with `queued_tick` = current `T`. Any rejection appends one result record and returns; nothing is thrown. The counter advances on every submit including rejected ones, so locally stamped values are dense (CR-4). **This order is normative** and goes into the kernel GDD (§ GDD sync) so tests are written against one order. It differs from CR-5's prose in one observable way: the type is resolved before the kernel-state check, because the `allowed_when_paused` exemption (CR-16) needs the type, so an unknown type submitted while `PAUSED` is `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, not `PAUSED`. The capacity check comes after coalescing because a supersession can free room.

`Command` is a `RefCounted` record with typed fields (`type_idx`, `issuer_peer`, `origin`, `actor`, `seq`, `correlation`, `payload`, `queued_tick`, `submission_id`, `host_order`) plus two kernel-only fields, `_sealed` and `_slot` (the `submission_id` it was admitted under). **Only `_admit` fills it, and only the queue owns the instances.** GDScript cannot make a constructor private, so the rule is enforced twice: at run time, `_admit` sets `_sealed = true` after filling a `Command` and records its `submission_id` in `_slot`, and the dispatch path (P1, P2, apply) refuses any `Command` that is unsealed or whose `_slot` does not match the queue entry it came from; and a CI check greps for `Command.new()` outside `src/kernel/`. `Command` has no `_init` parameter for `issuer_peer` at all. This is the "no constructor without `issuer_peer` exists" rule (kernel H6) in a form GDScript can state.

**No object is reused.** The ring holds references to `Command` instances; each admitted submit allocates one (a few tens per second, negligible, and the same order as the `var_to_bytes` allocation the size check already accepts); a slot is released by assigning `null`. Nothing pools or recycles a `Command`, so no `validate`, `apply`, result record or log entry can see a reused object. Even so, **owners must not retain `cmd` past the callable it was passed to** (copy the scalar fields needed), and **result and log records copy the scalar fields they need rather than holding a `Command`**. The command log copies the payload bytes.

Command types are addressed by `StringName` in the call and resolved once to a small integer `type_idx` at registration; the hot path is one `Dictionary` lookup keyed by `StringName`.

### 3. Payload schema per command type, enforced at admission

The kernel GDD checks payloads against a recursive `Variant.Type` whitelist (finite floats, depth ≤ 8, uniform dictionary key type, size ≤ 4 KiB via `var_to_bytes(payload).size()`). That says what a payload may be made of, not what a given command carries. This ADR adds a **mandatory `payload_schema`** to the command-type descriptor:

```gdscript
# Keys are the payload dictionary keys; values describe the expected value.
payload_schema = {
	&"target": {&"type": TYPE_INT, &"required": true},
	&"face_octant": {&"type": TYPE_INT, &"required": false, &"min": 0, &"max": 8},
}
```

**Order of the payload checks.** (1) The whitelist walk: `typeof()` against a constant set of allowed `Variant.Type`s, every dictionary key a `StringName` for payload dictionaries (a `String` key is `MALFORMED`, so the schema lookup is exact), all keys of any nested dictionary of one type, depth cap `PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH` 8, `is_finite()` on every float and on every component of `Vector2` and each element of the float and `Vector2` packed arrays, and a running upper-bound byte estimate that aborts the walk the moment it exceeds `MAX_PAYLOAD`. (2) Only after the walk passes, `var_to_bytes(payload).size() <= MAX_PAYLOAD`. (3) The schema below. A cyclic container is rejected by the depth cap at step 1, never serialised. Packed arrays are whitelisted and counted in the byte estimate (a large `PackedByteArray` passes the type check but not the budget). The range checks in step 3 test `is_finite()` first, because `NAN < min` and `NAN > max` are both false and a naive range test would pass `NAN`.

Admission checks, after the whitelist walk passes: every required key present; no key outside the schema; each value of the declared `Variant.Type` (an `int` where `float` is declared is `MALFORMED`, never silently converted); integers and floats inside the declared inclusive range when one is given. Entity and actor ids are `int` (64-bit in GDScript) and are non-negative; `NO_ACTOR` is `-1`, which no real id can equal. Ids above 2^53 must never pass through JSON (a JSON number parses as a float and loses precision); saves carry them as packed integer arrays (ADR-0006). A mismatch is `MALFORMED`. The dictionary form above is authoring syntax. At registration the kernel **compiles each schema into parallel arrays** (keys, types, required flags, bounds) and validates it at boot: an unknown schema key (a typo such as `&"minn"`) fails boot, and a bound whose type does not match the field's declared type fails boot (an `int` field with a `float` bound would otherwise compare silently). Admission then walks the compiled arrays, not nested dictionaries. The schema is **flat**: it covers the top-level keys of the payload. Nested `ARRAY`, `DICTIONARY` and packed values are checked **by type only** (the whitelist walk already checked element types, depth and key-type uniformity), and what their elements mean stays in the owner's `validate`; a later `elements` sub-schema is possible but not needed by the MVP commands (SYSTEM payloads such as `weld {actor, target, cause}` are flat). Payload dictionaries use `StringName` keys; a caller that writes `{"target": x}` produces a `String` key and is `MALFORMED`, so no lookup depends on `String`/`StringName` equivalence. The schema describes **shape only**; whether the target exists, is in reach or is lit stays in the owner's `validate`, so a rejection reason is never produced by the schema layer except `MALFORMED`. A type with no payload registers an explicit empty schema `{}` (no silent default, matching CR-6's rule for the other mandatory fields); omitting the field fails boot.

The schema is data on the descriptor, so the same table drives the admission check, the STRICT_DEBUG serialisation round-trip test, the control-manifest's list of commands, and the debug overlay's command panel.

### 4. Ownership is a kernel binding table keyed by PlayerId

Exactly as CR-7: half (a) `peer_id → PlayerId` is session state set by a host-only API (a boot step in the MVP: `HOST_PEER_ID` 1 → PlayerId 1), never touched by a restore, new game or death restart, and never resetting any issuer's `seq`. Half (b) `PlayerId → {(source block_id, entity_id)}` is derived from saved state and is never saved; the kernel rebuilds it as the last step of every pass through `LOADING` from the registered binding sources in ascending `block_id` order. The data structure:

- Half (a): a `Dictionary` `int → int`.
- Half (b): per PlayerId, one small `PlayerBindings` object holding two parallel `PackedInt64Array`s (source block index, entity id) behind one `add` / `remove` / `owns(source, entity)` interface, so the arrays cannot drift out of step. A player owns a handful of entities (an avatar and a beam), so `owns` is a linear scan of a few elements with no composite-key hashing and no allocation. Mutation is an explicit read-modify-write on the object's own arrays (never `dict[k].append(x)` on a packed array stored in a dictionary, whose behaviour has varied across versions), covered by a unit test.
- **Determinism of iteration.** The `LOADING` rebuild and every registry walk iterate **sorted** arrays (block ids ascending, command types in registration order recorded in an array), never `keys()` of a Dictionary filled from an unordered source. Dictionaries preserve insertion order in Godot 4, but erasing and re-inserting a key moves it to the end, so no hash or rebuild may depend on it.

A command type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` passes P2 iff `(actor_source(type), actor)` is in half (b) of `PlayerId(issuer_peer)`; otherwise it is `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)` with no state change. Persistent state is keyed by PlayerId; the peer id appears only in the ingress stamp and the binding table. Ownership is **never** derived from scene-tree node ownership, `set_multiplayer_authority()` or any engine multiplayer primitive.

### 5. Ordering, coalescing and the queue

- Apply order is ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`, where `host_order` is the arrival counter at `_admit`; in single-player it is submission order (CR-13 G1).
- The queue is one preallocated ring of `Command` slots sized to `QUEUE_CAPACITY` with per-issuer counters for `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` and a `SYSTEM_RESERVE` so SYSTEM commands cannot be starved by a flood of PLAYER ones. Overflow is `QUEUE_FULL` at admission, never a silent drop. **Accounting rule:** the capacity counters (`QUEUE_CAPACITY`, `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY`) decrement the moment a command is superseded, P1 skips tombstones and counts only live commands against `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`, and the tombstone's ring position is reclaimed when the head passes it, so an aim stream under backlog cannot cause a spurious `QUEUE_FULL`. On entry to `LOADING`, `SHUTTING_DOWN` or `FAULTED` the queue is flushed and every queued command receives `Dropped(RELOAD|SHUTDOWN|FAULTED)` (the exactly-one-result guarantee, CR-5 and G5).
- **Coalescing** (`coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`) is done by scanning the unfrozen portion of the queue for a command with the same `(type_idx, actor, issuer_peer)` and marking the older one `Superseded`. The scan runs only when a coalescing type is submitted, and intent types are sent a few times per second (aim at most every 3 ticks), so the scan over at most 1,024 slots is cheap and avoids a second index structure that would have to be kept in step with the ring. A type with `coalesce ≠ NONE` that allows both origins fails boot (`COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN`).
- Each tick, P1 moves at most `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` commands into the frozen batch for P2; the rest wait FIFO.
- A command older than its type's `max_age_ticks` is `STALE`. At local defaults this is unreachable (CR-17) and is guarded by an invariant test.

### 6. The control plane is a host-local API on a `ControlHandle`

`request_pause()`, `request_resume()`, `request_snapshot()`, `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)`, `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch)`, `request_shutdown()`, `request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)` are methods of `ControlHandle`, not commands. They are not stamped, queued, authority-checked or logged as commands. Each call is appended to a small host-local request list and served **at the next boundary service, in arrival order** (ADR-0001 § 1), and each request ends in exactly one outcome: `SERVED`, `DEFERRED` (made while an atomic step was active; evaluated at the first boundary after it) or `IGNORED` (a (state, trigger) pair the transition table does not list; one invalid-transition entry, no state change). **Outcome delivery.** Outcomes are always recorded in diagnostics. Callers that must act on one set `ControlHandle.set_outcome_handler(Callable)` and receive a typed `ControlOutcome` (`request_kind`, `outcome`, `tick`, and for `request_restore` the K-4 verdict `{T, computed_hash, verdict}` with `verdict` one of `MATCH`, `MISMATCH` or `NONE`; for `request_snapshot` the captured payload, a deep copy, plus the hash data listed below) at the same per-frame flush point as command results, **in a separate list that is never part of the CR-5 command result buffer**. This amends one sentence of the kernel GDD (States and Transitions, "control-plane requests have none"; § GDD sync): the outcome list is not a command result record, but it exists, because Save/Load needs the snapshot payload and the K-4 verdict (CR-15) and PauseGate needs to converge. **Snapshot outcome carries the hash data (amended 2026-10-28, TD-05).** `request_snapshot()` stays asynchronous and returns `void`; its result arrives only through the outcome handler. The snapshot `ControlOutcome` adds `T: int`, `world_seed: int`, `state_hash: int`, `hash_algo: int`, `block_ids: Array[StringName]`, `schema_versions: PackedInt64Array`, `block_state_hashes: PackedInt64Array` and `enc_lens: PackedInt64Array`. The four arrays are parallel (index `i` describes `block_ids[i]`), sorted by `block_id`, and cover **every persist block, WORLD and PROFILE**; all hashes and lengths are computed uncached inside `SAVING` (ADR-0005 § 4.7 and § 5.4). ADR-0005 owns what the hash values mean; this ADR owns only that they tra

Two consequences are intentional: a `request_pause` and a `request_resume` in the same boundary pair up in order, and `PauseGate` (Chart Table) re-issues the latest desired pause state until the kernel matches it, so a same-boundary pair leaves no wedged half-open state (TR-charttable-004).

**Seat binding (binding table half (a)).** `request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)` are the host-only writers of `peer_id → PlayerId` (CR-7). The composition root, holding the `game` control handle, calls `request_bind_seat(HOST_PEER_ID, 1)` as its boot step; the Co-op Session calls the same two methods in VS-B, so the kernel's public API does not widen then. A restore, new game or death restart never touches half (a). Runtime seat reassignment (kernel open question 4) is deferred to ADR-0032 under this signature. When `issuer_peer` has no half (a) entry, a type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` is `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)`; a `NONE` type proceeds.

Pause is single-player only. While `PAUSED` the kernel accepts only command types flagged `allowed_when_paused` whose `writes_blocks` name no `gameplay = true` block; everything else is rejected `PAUSED` at admission without queuing (CR-16). The control plane is host-local by construction: a remote ingress has no `ControlHandle`.

This ADR owns how requests are accepted, ordered and answered. The states they move between (`RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `LOADING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`) and the transitions' internals belong to ADR-0003.

### 7. Result delivery

Results are plain records (`result_id`, `issuer_peer`, `origin`, `seq`, `correlation`, `ok`, `reason`, `subject`, `detail`, `tick`) appended to the kernel's result buffer and flushed at P5 and once per rendered frame in every kernel state. A flush swaps the buffer out before delivering, so a handler that resubmits cannot recurse; it iterates that local array and re-checks each handler's validity per item, so a handler that frees its owner or its surface mid-flush invalidates only itself. `issue_surface_handle` and `issue_control_handle` are legal only in `BOOTING`, so a handler calling them mid-flush is a violation (CR-19), not a new handle. PLAYER results go to the issuing `SurfaceHandle`'s result handler and to the diagnostics log. SYSTEM results go to the command log and diagnostics counters only; an owner that needs an outcome reads state. Reason codes are computed from true state and never filtered by the kernel; whether and how cheaply a reason reaches the player is the presenter's rule (Pillar 4 cost rule), not this pipeline's.

### 8. HOST and MIRROR share one API; ingress is the only difference

On a MIRROR kernel `SurfaceHandle.submit` routes to an egress adapter (VS-B, ADR-0032), not to `_admit`; the handle's API is unchanged. `Kernel` is constructed with `Mode.HOST` or `Mode.MIRROR` and a `KernelProfile` (`STRICT_DEBUG` or `LENIENT_RELEASE`, injected, never read from `OS.is_debug_build()`). The public API is identical. A MIRROR does not tick and does not apply; it exists in the MVP only as a mode flag with a unit test proving `step()` refuses to apply in that mode. The ingress kinds are:

| Ingress | Origin it stamps | `issuer_peer` | May supply `seq` | Exists in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local surface handle | PLAYER | the handle's peer (`HOST_PEER_ID` = 1) | no | MVP |
| `submit_system` on a context | SYSTEM | `HOST_PEER_ID` | no | MVP |
| Test ingress | either | caller's choice | yes | tests only: lives under `tests/`, is injected by the harness, and is never named by a `class_name` that shipped code references (an export filter removes files, and a referenced missing class fails to load) |
| Remote ingress adapter | PLAYER, always (it has no origin parameter) | the network sender id, read only here | yes | VS-B (ADR-0032) |

The remote ingress adapter is the only place in the project that reads a network sender id, and `SYSTEM` commands never arrive from a network by construction: the adapter cannot stamp that origin.

### 9. Command log and STRICT_DEBUG

A bounded ring of `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY` records (command metadata, a copy of the payload bytes and the result) supports diagnostics and replay tests only; the log is not saved and is not the source of truth. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` every command is round-tripped through `var_to_bytes` / `bytes_to_var` before dispatch; one that cannot survive is a violation (CR-19). Under `LENIENT_RELEASE` the round trip is skipped and a violation is counted rather than faulting where the GDD allows it.
